quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.10-pre-review-codex.md:623:./docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:249:**Detail.** Design § 5.5 proposes adding `fn call_site(&self) -> CallSite` to `CellEnv`. But `CellEnv::formula_cell_for_sref(&self) -> Option<ql_types::Address>` (env.rs:83) already exists — it returns the formula's own cell address, defaulting to `None` for envs that don't carry one. `WorkbookEnv::with_formula_cell` (env.rs:140) sets it; the structured-ref `[@Col]` narrowing code already consumes it (scalar.rs:489).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:253:**Recommendation.** Reuse `formula_cell_for_sref()`. Rename in a follow-up if its current name (sref = structured-ref-specific connotation) becomes load-bearing for multiple consumers — but for v1, just call it. Drop the proposed `CallSite { sheet, row, col }` struct; pass `Address` (already exists, address.rs:35).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:356:The actual "cleaner" shape per the design depends on how dyn-friendly we want to keep `CellEnv`. Today `CellEnv` is used as `E: CellEnv` (generic), NOT `&dyn CellEnv` — the `narrow_structured_ref` signature uses `<E: CellEnv + ?Sized>`. So we DON'T need dyn-compatibility; we CAN have methods returning `&dyn ReferenceQuery`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-opus.md:414:3. **Structured-ref args** — `ROWS(Sales[Qty])` / `ROW(Sales[@Qty])` — the W5-115/117 structured-ref path materializes into either `AggregateNameRef`-equivalent (full column) or single-cell-narrowed (via formula_cell). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:431:### MEDIUM-S3-O-6 — No test for `ISFORMULA(<structured-ref>)`. The S1-HIGH-B / S2-HIGH-1 deferral of structured-ref tests to Step 5 doesn't fully apply to ISFORMULA — the eager-materializer's StructuredRef arm narrows via `narrow_structured_ref`, which behaves differently for `Sales[@Col]` (single-cell after narrowing) vs `Sales[Col]` (full column). ISFORMULA's single-cell path should query `is_formula_at`, multi-cell should return `#N/A`. The current impl is correct but unverified.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:440:1. `=ISFORMULA(Sales[@Qty])` where Sales is a table. The binder produces `ExprPlan::StructuredRef { resolved: full_col_range, is_this_row: true }`. The materializer's StructuredRef arm calls `narrow_structured_ref(resolved, true, env)` → returns a single-row range. `RefArg::Range { range: 1-row-range }`. **But the range may still be multi-COLUMN** (Sales[@Qty] is 1-row × 1-col if Qty is a single column). Need to verify the impl's 1×1 check (`range.start_row == range.end_row && range.start_col == range.end_col`) is satisfied for the typical narrow case.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:442:2. `=ISFORMULA(Sales[Qty])` (full column, no `@`). `is_this_row: false`, `narrow_structured_ref` returns the range unchanged. Multi-cell range → `#N/A`. Correct.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:444:The deferral in S2-HIGH-1 (structured-ref to Step 5 cross-cutting) is explicit, but the Step 3 ISFORMULA tests don't acknowledge this is deferred. The coverage entry says "covered by reference_fns unit tests (NoOpReferenceQuery FALSE path + arity + multi-cell #N/A + non-reference #N/A + error propagation) + ql-exec workbook-runtime e2e ..." — no mention of structured-ref deferral.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:450:2. Update the EXPLICITLY_DEFERRED entry to mention structured-ref coverage is deferred to Step 5.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:580:### LOW-O-8 — Coverage-matrix entry text is verbose and inconsistently structured across the 4 fns.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:138:Each `Locale` value carries: `arg_separator: char`, `decimal_separator: char`, `array_row_separator: char`, `array_col_separator: char`. **No `intersection_operator` field** — `@` is invariant across locales (it's also the structured-ref escape sentinel; locale-configuring `@` would break OOXML compat per Sonnet H-5).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:161:9. **Structured ref** — the `@` INSIDE `Sales[@Col]` is unrelated (different parser context; absorbed by `Token::StructuredRef`). The `@` BEFORE a structured ref like `=@Sales[Qty]` IS this operator: it narrows the column to the formula's row.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:268:| 8 | **4.9.H** (W5-144, shipped, binder-only — no ExprPlan variant) | Binder narrows `@expr` at BIND TIME per design § 3.3 (rules 1-9). Strategy refined during implementation: NO `ExprPlan::ImplicitIntersection` variant — every reachable case collapses to an existing ExprPlan shape, so the wrapper is dropped at bind. Mapping: rule 1 (scalar) → pass-through; rule 5 (single cell / `A1:A1`) → CellRef; rules 2/3 (single col/row range with anchor in span) → narrowed CellRef; rule 4 (2-D range) → `ExprPlan::Error(#VALUE!)`; rule 6 (WholeColumn/WholeRow) → narrowed CellRef (multi-col `A:C` → `#VALUE!`); rule 7 (array literal) → top-left literal; rule 8 (function) → bind inner as-is (scalar return passes through; array return is `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit, known gap); rule 9 (StructuredRef) → bind via `resolve_structured_ref` then patch `is_this_row: true` so eval narrows to formula row (makes `@Sales[Qty]` ≡ `Sales[@Qty]`). Nested `@@expr` collapses at bind via recursion. New `BindError::ImplicitIntersectionRequiresAnchor` fires for range narrowing without `site.cell`. **AST round-trip preserved** — printer still emits `@<inner>` per W5-143; only the eval plan drops the wrapper. **Known gaps** documented for cell-boundary spill rewiring (4.9.L): rule 7 for function-returned arrays, full rule-8 narrowing of array-returning functions, named-range narrowing for `Range`-resolving names. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:269:| 9 | **4.9.I** (W5-145, shipped) | Persistence v6 → v7. `WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION = 7`. **Two-phase load** (closes Sonnet H-2): new `SchemaVersionProbe { schema_version: u32 }` deserializes first (no `deny_unknown_fields`); the version-range check runs BEFORE the full `WorkbookEnvelope` deserialization, so a vN reader rejects vN+1 files cleanly without `deny_unknown_fields` confusion. New v7 fields `reference_mode: Option<ReferenceModeWire>` + `locale: Option<LocaleWire>` use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; loader maps `None` → A1 / EnUs. **Custom `LocaleWire` deserializer** (closes Sonnet M-2): unknown strings deserialize to `LocaleWire::Unknown(captured_string)`; loader surfaces `QbookError::UnknownLocale { found }`. **Post-deserialize forward-compat assertion** (closes Codex HIGH-5): if `schema_version < 7` AND either v7 field is set, return new `QbookError::ForwardCompatFieldOnOldVersion { schema_version, field }`. **Save-side minimal-TOML**: default A1/EnUs writes neither field. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:270:| 10 | **4.9.J** (W5-146, shipped) | Op log: `Op::SetReferenceMode { mode: ReferenceModeWire }` + `Op::SetLocale { locale: LocaleWire }` variants in `ql-oplog::op`. Replay arms call `Workbook::set_reference_mode` / `Workbook::set_locale`. **Custom `LocaleWire` deserializer** matches the W5-145 qbook v7 pattern: unknown strings captured to `LocaleWire::Unknown(s)`, surfaced via new `ReplayError::UnknownLocale { index, found }` (closes Sonnet L-10). Wire types `ReferenceModeWire` / `LocaleWire` re-exported from `ql_oplog::` for use by the runtime API and downstream consumers. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:296:- **Persistence v6 → v7** — additive envelope fields + two-phase load. v6 reader rejects v7 via version check (not via `deny_unknown_fields`).

Mapping: rule 1 (scalar) → pass-through; rule 5 (single cell / `A1:A1`) → CellRef; rules 2/3 (single col/row range with anchor in span) → narrowed CellRef; rule 4 (2-D range) → `ExprPlan::Error(#VALUE!)`; rule 6 (WholeColumn/WholeRow) → narrowed CellRef (multi-col `A:C` → `#VALUE!`); rule 7 (array literal) → top-left literal; rule 8 (function) → bind inner as-is (scalar return passes through; array return is `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit, known gap); rule 9 (StructuredRef) → bind via `resolve_structured_ref` then patch `is_this_row: true` so eval narrows to formula row (makes `@Sales[Qty]` ≡ `Sales[@Qty]`). Nested `@@expr` collapses at bind via recursion. New `BindError::ImplicitIntersectionRequiresAnchor` fires for range narrowing without `site.cell`. **AST round-trip preserved** — printer still emits `@<inner>` per W5-143; only the eval plan drops the wrapper. **Known gaps** documented for cell-boundary spill rewiring (4.9.L): rule 7 for function-returned arrays, full rule-8 narrowing of array-returning functions, named-range narrowing for `Range`-resolving names. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:958:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:834:./docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:183:| 9 | **4.9.I** (W5-145, shipped) | Persistence v6 → v7. `WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION = 7`. **Two-phase load** (closes Sonnet H-2): new `SchemaVersionProbe { schema_version: u32 }` deserializes first (no `deny_unknown_fields`); the version-range check runs BEFORE the full `WorkbookEnvelope` deserialization, so a vN reader rejects vN+1 files cleanly without `deny_unknown_fields` confusion. New v7 fields `reference_mode: Option<ReferenceModeWire>` + `locale: Option<LocaleWire>` use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`; loader maps `None` → A1 / EnUs. **Custom `LocaleWire` deserializer** (closes Sonnet M-2): unknown strings deserialize to `LocaleWire::Unknown(captured_string)`; loader surfaces `QbookError::UnknownLocale { found }`. **Post-deserialize forward-compat assertion** (closes Codex HIGH-5): if `schema_version < 7` AND either v7 field is set, return new `QbookError::ForwardCompatFieldOnOldVersion { schema_version, field }`. **Save-side minimal-TOML**: default A1/EnUs writes neither field. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex-retry.md:959:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:835:./docs/architecture/2026-05-15-r1c1-locales-implicit-intersection.md:184:| 10 | **4.9.J** (W5-146, shipped) | Op log: `Op::SetReferenceMode { mode: ReferenceModeWire }` + `Op::SetLocale { locale: LocaleWire }` variants in `ql-oplog::op`. Replay arms call `Workbook::set_reference_mode` / `Workbook::set_locale`. **Custom `LocaleWire` deserializer** matches the W5-145 qbook v7 pattern: unknown strings captured to `LocaleWire::Unknown(s)`, surfaced via new `ReplayError::UnknownLocale { index, found }` (closes Sonnet L-10). Wire types `ReferenceModeWire` / `LocaleWire` re-exported from `ql_oplog::` for use by the runtime API and downstream consumers. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3593:docs/MASTER-PLAN.md:495:   **Status (2026-05-15): SHIPPED triple-confirmed at `6523001b837` (W5-152).** All 15 sub-phases shipped (AA design + A types + B.1-.4 lexer + C parser+binder + D printer + F locale-printer + G `@`-parser-printer + H `@`-binder + I persistence v6→v7 + J op-log + K runtime+canonical + L round-trip + M coverage matrix + N polish + O closing megaudit). Acceptance closures: LOC-4-01 R1C1 round-trips pinned at lex/parse/bind/print stages; LOC-4-02 EN/DE/FR separators pinned by 30-cell coverage matrix; LOC-4-03 `@` operator + design § 3.3 9-rule narrowing implemented at bind time; LOC-4-04 `WorkbookRuntime::set_reference_mode` + `set_locale` APIs available. Closing megaudit (three-way: self-review + Sonnet + Codex async) found 1 HIGH (PlanCache × `@<range>` cell collision — fixed W5-150) + 2 MEDIUM (W5-151) + 3 LOW (W5-152). +175 net tests (2443 → 2618). Function-name localization remained OUT-of-scope per LOC-4-02 (separators only). Known gaps documented: rule 7 (array-returning function under `@` returns `#CALC!` per existing 4.7.G limit) → cell-boundary spill rewiring; cross-sheet structured refs (`Sheet1.Sales[Qty]`) → later Phase. Full audit trail in `docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-*.md`.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3628:docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3763:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:20:5. **Mutation API** — `WorkbookRuntime::create_table`, `rename_table`, `rename_column`, `resize_table`, `drop_table`. Each emits a corresponding op-log entry.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3764:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:164:Decision: use `Arc<str>` (uppercase canonical) as the primary key, matching `NameTable`. A separate `TableId(u32)` is tempting for the graph (stable across renames) but adds complexity. **Renames REWRITE formula text** (Excel canon, see § 12.2). The plan-cache-invalidation alternative (the original draft's approach) was broken: cached plans rebind against the OLD name and fail `BindError::UnknownTable`, breaking bind/recompute/persistence. Rewrite-on-rename is the simpler correct path.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3765:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:608:**Formula text IS rewritten on rename** (Excel canon). The original draft proposed plan-cache invalidation + no rewrite — Codex correctly noted that cached plans rebind against the OLD name and fail `BindError::UnknownTable`, breaking bind/recompute/persistence.

Phase 4.8 ships without it; current behavior is hard-reject at `set_formula`. Fresh-session work, needs explicit user sign-off on the contract change before implementation. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3767:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:713:2. **4.8.N soft-fail** — backwards-incompatible API contract change. Currently `set_formula("SUM(Sales[Qty])")` BEFORE `create_table("Sales", ...)` hard-rejects with `BindError::UnknownTable`. Design § 7.4 wants accept-text-and-surface-error-cell-value with re-bind on `on_table_create`. Needs explicit sign-off on the contract change before implementation.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:3940:docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-megaudit-opus-a.md:257:**Severity**: MEDIUM (documented behavior, but the public-API doc string says "on first failure abort the whole import", implying any error fails — users wanting strict will be surprised that an unknown-function formula evaluates to `Value::Error(Name)` which Strict considers success).

The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:4304:docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:1602:docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:4306:docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2103:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:164:Decision: use `Arc<str>` (uppercase canonical) as the primary key, matching `NameTable`. A separate `TableId(u32)` is tempting for the graph (stable across renames) but adds complexity. **Renames REWRITE formula text** (Excel canon, see § 12.2). The plan-cache-invalidation alternative (the original draft's approach) was broken: cached plans rebind against the OLD name and fail `BindError::UnknownTable`, breaking bind/recompute/persistence. Rewrite-on-rename is the simpler correct path.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:4307:docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2127:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:608:**Formula text IS rewritten on rename** (Excel canon). The original draft proposed plan-cache invalidation + no rewrite — Codex correctly noted that cached plans rebind against the OLD name and fail `BindError::UnknownTable`, breaking bind/recompute/persistence.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-b-codex.md:4353:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-design-review-codex.md:332:   147	3. **`@` operator precedence + disambiguation** — `=@SUM(...)` (implicit intersection of function result) vs `=Sales[@Col]` (structured-ref `@`). The parser context matters: inside `[...]` of a structured ref, `@` means "this row"; outside, `@` means implicit intersection. How to teach the parser this without breaking the existing structured-ref escape rules from 4.8.D?

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:160:**Why M:** The envelope is TOML which is largely whitespace-tolerant, so dropping a trailing newline (typical "last byte") still parses. The bigger picture: there's no envelope-level checksum, so a flipped byte in the *middle* of `workbook.toml` that happens to keep TOML syntactically valid would load to a silently-wrong workbook. The existing two-phase load (`SchemaVersionProbe` first, then `WorkbookEnvelope` with `deny_unknown_fields`) is good defense against schema drift but not against value corruption.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:201:- No PANICs across 12 `.qbook` corruption probes — every form of corruption (truncated TOML, random bytes, wrong schema version, malformed JSONL, missing files, not-a-directory) surfaces a typed `QbookError`. Two-phase load (probe schema_version first, then deserialize with `deny_unknown_fields`) is doing its job.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-2-opus.md:39:Detail: W5-D-2 introduces a new lexer code path (the `if next_is_digit` branch starting at line 552) and a new error condition (the `saw_letter` check at line 569 — pure-digit segments rejected). The implementing commit adds *zero* `#[test]` functions in `lexer::tests` to pin this new behavior. The only happy-path coverage is the e2e tests in `distribution_fns_e2e.rs` (e.g. `t_dist_case_insensitive_lookup_works` which exercises `t.dist.2t`/`t.dist.rt`). A future refactor of `lex_ident_or_ref` could regress the digit-leading branch and the only failures would surface as "T.DIST.2T (unknown function)"-style errors in the e2e suite, not in lexer tests where regressions belong.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:38:Add calcgraph tests covering direct-cell suppression, scalar fallback dependencies, named-range retargeting, and structured-reference table changes.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:46:Subject: ROW/COLUMN cell-boundary guard misses structured references
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:54:The eager materializer later turns a structured reference into `RefArg::Range` through `narrow_structured_ref`. Therefore a top-level formula such as `ROW(Sales[Qty])` or `COLUMN(Sales[Qty])` can bypass the boundary guard and execute with only the materialized range coordinates. If the Step 2 implementation returns the top-left row/column, this recreates the silent truncation behavior the design is trying to prevent.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:56:The guard also needs to distinguish full-column structured references from narrowed `[@...]` forms. A blanket `StructuredRef` rejection would incorrectly reject cases that narrow to a single cell or single row at the formula cell.

Default `Disabled` (preserves V2 V1 behavior); `OnAppend` triggers `flush_to_transport` after every mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`, `update_presence`, `clear_presence`, `sweep_presence`, `undo`, `redo`). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v2-codex.md:462:docs/architecture/ide-consumer-contract.md:207:- **Auto-flush (✅ Phase 5.5 V2 V2 SHIPPED 2026-05-21):** `CollabSession::set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend)` makes every mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`, presence writes, `undo`, `redo`, `sweep_presence`) auto-invoke `flush_to_transport` after a successful state change. IDE callers can drop their scheduled-flush-tick loops. Default is `AutoFlushPolicy::Disabled` (V2 V1 explicit-drive behavior preserved — set explicitly to opt in). **Partial-state contract**: if auto-flush fails (closed transport, I/O error), the surrounding mutator returns `Err(CollabSessionError::Transport(_))` BUT the local op is already committed (mutate-then-flush ordering). Callers MUST treat local state as authoritative + either retry the flush or detach the transport. The explicit `flush_to_transport` API remains available regardless of policy (mix-and-match supported).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v2-codex.md:2322:   207	- **Auto-flush (✅ Phase 5.5 V2 V2 SHIPPED 2026-05-21):** `CollabSession::set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend)` makes every mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`, presence writes, `undo`, `redo`, `sweep_presence`) auto-invoke `flush_to_transport` after a successful state change. IDE callers can drop their scheduled-flush-tick loops. Default is `AutoFlushPolicy::Disabled` (V2 V1 explicit-drive behavior preserved — set explicitly to opt in). **Partial-state contract**: if auto-flush fails (closed transport, I/O error), the surrounding mutator returns `Err(CollabSessionError::Transport(_))` BUT the local op is already committed (mutate-then-flush ordering). Callers MUST treat local state as authoritative + either retry the flush or detach the transport. The explicit `flush_to_transport` API remains available regardless of policy (mix-and-match supported).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v2-codex.md:2338:   584	   - **V2 V2 ✅ SHIPPED 2026-05-21**: `AutoFlushPolicy::{Disabled, OnAppend}` enum + `set_auto_flush_policy` + `auto_flush_policy` accessors on `CollabSession`. Default `Disabled` (preserves V2 V1 behavior); `OnAppend` triggers `flush_to_transport` after every mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`, `update_presence`, `clear_presence`, `sweep_presence`, `undo`, `redo`). Partial-state contract on flush failure documented per CLAUDE.md No-Fallback rule.

Default `Disabled` (preserves V2 V1 behavior); `OnAppend` triggers `flush_to_transport` after every mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`, `update_presence`, `clear_presence`, `sweep_presence`, `undo`, `redo`). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v2-codex.md:2722:docs/architecture/ide-consumer-contract.md:207:- **Auto-flush (✅ Phase 5.5 V2 V2 SHIPPED 2026-05-21):** `CollabSession::set_auto_flush_policy(AutoFlushPolicy::OnAppend)` makes every mutator (`append_op`, `merge_bytes`, presence writes, `undo`, `redo`, `sweep_presence`) auto-invoke `flush_to_transport` after a successful state change. IDE callers can drop their scheduled-flush-tick loops. Default is `AutoFlushPolicy::Disabled` (V2 V1 explicit-drive behavior preserved — set explicitly to opt in). **Partial-state contract**: if auto-flush fails (closed transport, I/O error), the surrounding mutator returns `Err(CollabSessionError::Transport(_))` BUT the local op is already committed (mutate-then-flush ordering). Callers MUST treat local state as authoritative + either retry the flush or detach the transport. The explicit `flush_to_transport` API remains available regardless of policy (mix-and-match supported).

quantbook-engine/docs/process/audit-protocol.md:13:Lock down the practices that keep the engine shipping correct, honest, auditable code across sessions. The biggest risk is silent doc/code divergence becoming the next window's starting premise — that already almost happened in W5-50 (`on_clear_formula` clear-path bug shipped under "GAP-G-01 closed" framing; caught only by the W5-52 parallel mega-audit). This protocol prevents that.

quantbook-engine/docs/process/audit-protocol.md:257:If you register a range-aware function via the scalar `register(...)` method by accident, it SILENTLY loses range shape: the dispatch builds flat `Vec<Value>` from a flattened range, the function gets a list of Values without per-arg structure, and SUMIF-style semantics break in subtle ways.
quantbook-engine/docs/process/audit-protocol.md:302:### 16. CHOOSE with a Range argument silently returns `#VALUE!` (Sonnet MEDIUM 2, W5-60)
quantbook-engine/docs/process/audit-protocol.md:312:The split fixes Codex HIGH H1 (bounded ranges silently shrunk under clamp, breaking trailing-blank semantics in lookups). Any future change to `read_range_with_shape` must preserve this branch.
quantbook-engine/docs/process/audit-protocol.md:316:`parse_ifs_pairs` and SUMPRODUCT now track 2D `(rows, cols)` shape, not flat length. A `2×2` range and a `1×4` range have the same flat length (4) but different shapes — Excel returns `#VALUE!`. Pre-W5-60 they would silently zip. If you add a new IFS-family function, use `parse_ifs_pairs`. If you write a new array-consensus function, follow SUMPRODUCT's pattern of tracking `Vec<(&[Value], usize, usize)>` with `(rows, cols)` consensus.

quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:78:| GAP-F-09 | `NETWORKDAYS` holidays-array arg not supported in V1. Excel canon: 3rd arg is an optional range of holiday dates that are subtracted from the working-day count. Quantbook's `ContextAwareFn` tier signature (`fn(&[Value], &EvalContext) -> Value`) has pre-evaluated scalar args only — range args silently lose shape (or surface as `#CALC!`). Supporting holidays needs a 4th registry tier `RangeAndContextAwareFn = fn(&[FnArg], &EvalContext) -> Value`. V1: 3-arg call returns `#VALUE!`. | `crates/ql-functions/src/date_fns.rs::networkdays_ctx`; pinned by `networkdays_with_holidays_arg_is_value_error_v1_divergence` | Engine | Engine Phase 4.5.C (when tier-4 lands) or 4.7 array formulas trigger |
quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |
quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:84:| GAP-F-13 | `FormatTable` pre-seeds only 18 of the 0-163 Excel built-in format ids (mini-spec § 10 parser-relevant subset). xlsx import (Phase 4.11) will commonly surface ids 5-8 (currency variants), 38 (red-negative-thousands), 41-44 (accounting), 46-47 (elapsed time variants), which would currently surface as `MalformedFormat` or render as `General` fallback. **Decision (W5-84):** pre-seed the full 0-163 table BEFORE xlsx import lands. Tracked here so the work isn't forgotten. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM); `crates/ql-storage/src/format.rs::BUILTIN_FORMATS` | Engine | Engine Phase 4.11 (xlsx) prerequisite |

quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:143:| IFS | ✅ | 6 | 4.10.A | W5-163: variadic test+value pairs; first true wins. Errors in tests propagate. No match → #N/A. Odd arg count silently discards trailing unpaired arg (matches Excel canon). Empty → #VALUE!. Non-bool tests coerce via `to_logical`. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:177:| SIN / COS / TAN / ASIN / ACOS / ATAN / ATAN2 | ✅ | 13 | 4.3 V2 | W5-51; ATAN2 uses Excel `(x, y)` arg order (not Rust's `(y, x)`); ATAN2(0,0)→#DIV/0!; ASIN/ACOS domain `|x|>1`→#NUM!; TAN(π/2) returns huge-finite (Excel canon, not error). **W5-D-13.1 megaudit closure (Codex HIGH-002 / Opus HIGH-2):** ATAN2 was previously unreachable from formula source (`ATAN2(1,1)` lex-errored with `ColumnTooLarge("ATAN")` — 4-letter prefix exceeded the 3-letter column-ref limit). The W5-D-13.1 lexer letters>3+digit Ident-fallback now emits `Ident("ATAN2")` so the parser dispatches correctly. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:191:| SUMX2MY2 / SUMX2PY2 / SUMXMY2 | ✅ | 9 | 4.10.D | W5-166: paired array sum-of-squares variants. RangeAwareFn; both args must be ranges; W5-60 strict 2D-shape check (shape mismatch → #VALUE!). Non-numeric cells coerce to 0 (lenient, matches IronCalc canon). Errors in either array propagate. **W5-D-13.1 megaudit closure (Codex HIGH-002 / Opus HIGH-2):** SUMXMY2 was previously unreachable from formula source (`SUMXMY2(...)` lex-errored with `ColumnTooLarge("SUMXMY")`). The W5-D-13.1 lexer letters>3+digit Ident-fallback fixed it. SUMX2MY2 / SUMX2PY2 were already reachable via the W5-D-9 letters-digits-letters extension. Also admitted to `is_aggregate_function` in W5-D-13.1 for named-range arg support. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:234:| DAYS / DAYS360 / NETWORKDAYS / NETWORKDAYS.INTL | ⚠️ | (see DATE row) | 4.5 V2 (W5-75) | W5-D-13.1: DAYS, DAYS360, NETWORKDAYS registered. **NETWORKDAYS.INTL not registered** (locale-aware variant — defer). DAYS360 was previously also blocked at lex time (4-letter prefix); W5-D-13.1 lexer Ident-fallback closure makes it reachable from source text. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:254:| ROW | ✅ | 9+8 e2e | RT-V1-01 Step 2 (W5-RT-2) | W5-RT-2: 1-indexed row of arg's top-left cell (Reference / Range / single-cell Range), or calling cell's row if omitted. Multi-cell range arg in scalar context returns top-left row (Excel pre-365 implicit-intersection); at cell-boundary `#CALC!` (S1-HIGH-B/E guard prevents silent truncation). `ROW(#REF!)` → `#REF!` (HIGH-F). Array literal → `#VALUE!` in scalar context. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:298:| IRR | ✅ | 6 | 4.10.F | W5-168: Newton-Raphson around guess (default 0.1), bisection fallback over `[-0.99999, 100]`, 50 iterations max, eps=1e-8 / 1e-10. Requires sign-change in cash-flow → otherwise `#NUM!`. Non-numeric cells in range → `#VALUE!` (stricter than NPV per IronCalc canon). |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:301:| XIRR | ✅ | 12 | Wave 3 closure (W5-D-7) | W5-D-7: date-indexed IRR via Newton-Raphson on `compute_xnpv` derivative; bisection fallback on [-0.9999, 100]; final Newton-Raphson at guess=200 if bisection misses. RangeAwareFn 2-3 args (values + dates + [guess=0.1]). At least one positive AND one negative value required (else #NUM!). Microsoft canonical anchor → ≈0.3734 (37.34%) pinned. Round-trip XNPV(xirr_result, ...) ≈ 0 pinned. Empty cells in values default to 0.0 (XIRR-specific divergence from XNPV's strict rejection). Text → #VALUE!. |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:304:| SYD | ✅ | 10 | 4.10 polish | W5-180 + W5-182.1: sum-of-years digits depreciation. ScalarFn. Formula: `(cost − salvage) · (life − per + 1) · 2 / (life · (life + 1))`. **Asymmetric degenerate-case canon with SLN**: SYD `life = 0` → `#NUM!` (NOT `#DIV/0!`). W5-182.1 audit closure (Opus MEDIUM-2): this asymmetry is **IronCalc convention**, not documented Microsoft canon — Microsoft's SYD doc is silent on the error code for `life = 0`. `per <= 0` or `per > life` → `#NUM!`. `per = life` boundary is valid (the rule is `>`, not `>=`). Pinned by `syd_sum_over_periods_equals_total_depreciation` invariant test: Σ SYD over k=1..life = (cost − salvage). |
quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:306:| DB | ✅ | 22 | 4.10 polish | W5-182 + W5-182.1: fixed-declining-balance depreciation. ScalarFn, 4-5 args (`month` defaults to 12, truncated to integer **before** validation — so `month = 12.9` truncates to 12 and passes; `month = 0.5` truncates to 0 and is rejected). **Period-iterating** (each period depends on accumulated book value) — unlike DDB which is closed-form. Excel-specific 3-decimal rate rounding: `rate = round((1 − (salvage/cost)^(1/life)) · 1000) / 1000` deliberately introduces per-period error absorbed by the last-partial-period. First period uses `month/12` fraction; last period (`period = life + 1` and `month ≠ 12`) uses complementary `(12 − month)/12` fraction. Validation (W5-182.1 audit closures expanded): `month == 12 && period > life`, `period > life + 1`, `month <= 0`, `month > 12`, `period < 1` (W5-182.1: tightened from `<= 0` after Opus MEDIUM-6 — fractional `period < 1` silently returned period-2's value), `cost < 0`, `life <= 0` (W5-182.1: Codex HIGH-1 — `DB(1000, 100, 0, 1, 7)` previously returned 583.33), `life > i32::MAX || period > i32::MAX` (W5-182.1: DoS-class — Opus MEDIUM-7), all → `#NUM!`. `cost == 0` short-circuits to `0` (avoiding `(salvage/0)` NaN). **Engine-convention divergence vs IronCalc (W5-182.1 Codex MEDIUM-1 / Opus MEDIUM-3)**: IronCalc rejects Boolean for `month` via `get_number_no_bools`; our `arg_num` allows Boolean uniformly. **Fractional-life IronCalc-inherited quirk (W5-182.1 Opus MEDIUM-4)**: rate uses raw `life`, iteration uses `life.floor()` — internally inconsistent for fractional `life`; documented but not fixed without verified Excel behavior. |

quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:160:6. **Table footprint fits within the Excel address grid** — NEW W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 closure, Codex HIGH-1). `top_row + rows - 1` must be `≤ MAX_ROW` (1,048,575) and `top_col + cols - 1` must be `≤ MAX_COLUMN` (16,383). `TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds` (in `ql-storage`) is the shared check; called at FIVE entry points: producer `create_table` / `resize_table`, replay `apply_create_table` / `apply_resize_table`, and v6 `.qbook` loader. Pre-W5-125 the check was missing, so `for r in top_row..top_row + rows` either ran past the addressable grid (registering cells later `Sheet::put` would panic on) or u32-overflowed silently (skipping all downstream overlap / spill-anchor checks).
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:545:Replay validates each op against current state; collisions (e.g., `CreateTable` for a name that already exists) surface as `ReplayError::TableCollision` (no silent overwrite). Op log atomicity per the Phase 4.7.J HIGH-3 pattern: append BEFORE mutation; failed append leaves workbook unchanged.
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:558:- **v5 reader loading v6 file**: the existing reader bound `v4..=WORKBOOK_SCHEMA_VERSION` REFUSES v6. **This is correct**: silently dropping table metadata would break formulas (a formula referencing `Sales[Qty]` would surface `BindError::UnknownTable` after load → cell renders `#NAME?` when pre-save it was a valid SUM). Loud refusal preserves semantic integrity.
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:643:1. **No fallbacks** — unknown table / column / specifier surfaces a specific bind error (per CLAUDE.md "errors must be visible"). Table-related bind errors map to cell error values per § 7.4 (so a formula referencing a not-yet-created table is accepted with an error cell value; later `create_table` dirties + re-binds).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-4-codex.md:8103:quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/ide-consumer-contract.md:183:- **The IDE does NOT call `Workbook::set_name`, `Workbook::add_sheet`, `Workbook::put_at`, or `Workbook::clear_formula` directly.** Those are LOW-LEVEL methods (doc-marked Phase 2B.5) used by the qbook loader, the op-log replay path, runtime-internal recompute pass 2, and tests. Direct calls bypass the op log silently — a correctness hole for product code.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-4-codex.md:8254:quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:160:6. **Table footprint fits within the Excel address grid** — NEW W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 closure, Codex HIGH-1). `top_row + rows - 1` must be `≤ MAX_ROW` (1,048,575) and `top_col + cols - 1` must be `≤ MAX_COLUMN` (16,383). `TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds` (in `ql-storage`) is the shared check; called at FIVE entry points: producer `create_table` / `resize_table`, replay `apply_create_table` / `apply_resize_table`, and v6 `.qbook` loader. Pre-W5-125 the check was missing, so `for r in top_row..top_row + rows` either ran past the addressable grid (registering cells later `Sheet::put` would panic on) or u32-overflowed silently (skipping all downstream overlap / spill-anchor checks).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-4-codex.md:10770:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-16-phase-4.8.G.3-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2102:docs/architecture/2026-05-14-structured-references-and-tables.md:160:6. **Table footprint fits within the Excel address grid** — NEW W5-125 (Phase 4.8.O.1 closure, Codex HIGH-1). `top_row + rows - 1` must be `≤ MAX_ROW` (1,048,575) and `top_col + cols - 1` must be `≤ MAX_COLUMN` (16,383). `TableMetadata::validate_footprint_bounds` (in `ql-storage`) is the shared check; called at FIVE entry points: producer `create_table` / `resize_table`, replay `apply_create_table` / `apply_resize_table`, and v6 `.qbook` loader. Pre-W5-125 the check was missing, so `for r in top_row..top_row + rows` either ran past the addressable grid (registering cells later `Sheet::put` would panic on) or u32-overflowed silently (skipping all downstream overlap / spill-anchor checks).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.B-codex-review.txt:142:All rows must have the same number of cells. Mismatched-row literals (e.g. `{1, 2; 3}`) error at parse time with `ParseError::ArrayRowArityMismatch { expected, found, row }`. **This is a Quantbook v1 subset** — Excel pads with `#N/A` for missing cells, and `{1,2;3}` evaluates as `{1,2;3,#N/A}`. Quantbook v1 chooses loud rejection over silent padding; the pad-with-`#N/A` variant is a Phase 4.10 polish item gated on test-corpus completeness.

quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-13-coercion-matrix.md:20:1. **Existing coercion code is well-built but ad-hoc helpers have proliferated.** `ql-types::coercion` centralizes 5 public functions (`to_number_strict`, `to_number_lenient`, `to_logical`, `to_text_for_display`, `to_text_for_formula`, plus the `sanitize_f64` overflow leaf). However, three private helpers (`scalar_fns::coerce_numeric` (×2 — duplicated across `scalar_fns.rs` and `range_fns.rs`), `scalar_fns::coerce_text`, `scalar_fns::coerce_int_arg`) wrap the centralized fns to support function-arg patterns that the central module doesn't directly express (Blank-skip in aggregates, position/length integer extraction, text-result fallback). These helpers are correct individually but have drifted slightly between callers — e.g. the W5-60 audit caught that not all 2D-shape-aware fns handled `FnArg::Range` vs `FnArg::Scalar` consistently.
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-13-coercion-matrix.md:107:| `=IFERROR(#REF!, 0)`                        | `0` (IFERROR catches) | [CURRENT][CANON] — args are pre-evaluated; IFERROR introspects the value and returns the fallback. FN4-03 is about lazy evaluation (not evaluating the FALLBACK if condition succeeds), NOT this simple introspection. |
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-13-coercion-matrix.md:180:- **Excel's "skip text and blanks in range" canon for SUM/AVERAGE/MIN/MAX**. Documented Quantbook V1 divergence — current behavior propagates `#VALUE!` for any text cell in a range arg (via `coerce_numeric` → `to_number_strict`), while Excel SILENTLY SKIPS text cells in range positions. ERROR cells in range correctly propagate in BOTH Excel and Quantbook — that's not the divergence. Codex review flagged the previous wording in this section was misframed; corrected. Defending V1 behavior: strict-text-in-range is easier for users to debug (no silent type-confusion bug masking), at the cost of one-step-extra to use `=SUMIF(A:A, ">0")` instead of `=SUM(A:A)` over text-bearing ranges.
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/ide-consumer-contract.md:75:- The workbook is unchanged (no partial write, per the no-fallbacks rule).
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/ide-consumer-contract.md:183:- **The IDE does NOT call `Workbook::set_name`, `Workbook::add_sheet`, `Workbook::put_at`, or `Workbook::clear_formula` directly.** Those are LOW-LEVEL methods (doc-marked Phase 2B.5) used by the qbook loader, the op-log replay path, runtime-internal recompute pass 2, and tests. Direct calls bypass the op log silently — a correctness hole for product code.
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/ide-consumer-contract.md:212:- **Offline-write (✅ Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 3 SHIPPED 2026-05-21)**: append while no transport attached → `append_op` returns `Ok(())` and commits locally; `maybe_auto_flush` silently no-ops. **Loro's CRDT op log IS the implicit offline queue — no separate buffer needed.** On reattach: `attach_transport` resets `last_flushed_vv = None`. The next mutator (or explicit `flush_delta_to_transport`) sends the delta from empty VV — delivers ALL accumulated ops including the offline ones. Recovery from a failed flush (transport closed mid-session) follows the same pattern: the failed-flush op is committed locally; detach + reattach (or just reattach — it replaces + resets) + explicit flush sends everything. NEW `CollabSession::has_pending_flush() -> bool` ergonomic helper: compares `current_vv` vs `last_flushed_vv.unwrap_or_default()`. Use for IDE status indicators ("Synced" vs "Unsynced changes") + reconnect handshake logic. **Idiom for explicit reattach-then-sync**: `session.attach_transport(t); if session.has_pending_flush() { session.flush_delta_to_transport()?; }` — `attach_transport` doesn't auto-flush by design (lifecycle event, not mutation; preserves V2 V1 `Option<previous>` return signature).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:23:**Cite:** `crates/ql-exec/src/plan.rs:233-240`; `crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime.rs:2542-2562`. W5-61 broke that contract silently.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:37:Excel itself has bounded-time matching here (Excel's matcher is iterative); this divergence is invisible until someone actually exploits it. Filing as HIGH because (i) it's an unbounded-runtime path triggered by ordinary-looking user input, (ii) the W5-61 commit ships it as "production-ready Excel-canon wildcards" with no perf disclaimer, and (iii) Quantbook's larger story is "1M-row sheets that recompute fast" — exponential matching breaks that story silently.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:73:CONCERN-B in the audit brief specifically called these out. If the W5-61 commit prose claims "behavior-preserving rewrite", these are the exact contracts that need pinning to prevent a future refactor from silently regressing them. The W5-56 SEARCH ship may have had these tests; let me note that I greped `crates/ql-functions/src/scalar_fns.rs` for `search_empty\|search.*needle\|empty.*needle.*search` and got zero hits — neither the W5-56 ship nor W5-61 has them.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:93:`crates/ql-functions/src/range_fns.rs:1386-1394`. CONCAT flattens by iterating the `values` Vec in its natural order. The shape comes from `env.read_range_with_shape` at `crates/ql-exec/src/env.rs:144-189`, which populates `for row { for col { out.push(...) } }` — row-major (left-to-right within a row, then row-by-row). For `A1:B2` the order is `A1, B1, A2, B2`. **This matches Excel's CONCAT canon.** But the doc comment on line 1374 just says "row-major order" without explaining what that means for a 2D range. The test `concat_flattens_range` (line 2644) uses a 1×N range, so it doesn't exercise the 2D semantics. A future contributor refactoring `read_range_with_shape` could silently flip this to column-major and only smoke tests on real sheets would catch it.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:111:CONCERN-I in the brief flagged this. Each `SUMIF(A:A, "foo*", B:B)` recompiles `WildcardPattern` on every formula evaluation. The pattern is invariant of the data, so a per-formula compile + cache (keyed on the criteria text) would help. This was filed as deferred-perf by the brief; I confirm it's worth a GAP-F entry rather than silent deferral.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:13:### H-1: UpdateOriginal silently overwrites the original theme/docProps with umya defaults
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:16:- Why it matters: I ran the existing test fixture (basic_text.xlsx) through `UpdateOriginal` and compared bytes. Original `xl/theme/theme1.xml` = 8390 bytes (Calibri Light + 30+ script-specific Office fonts). Output theme = 6518 bytes (umya default — different font roster, different effectStyleLst, no font script fallbacks). Original `docProps/core.xml` has `<dc:creator>Nicolas Hatcher</dc:creator>` + real `dcterms:modified` date `2023-01-22T01:26:39Z`. Output has empty `<dcterms:created>2006-09-16T00:00:00Z</dcterms:created>` (umya stub). The user-visible "Round-trip preserves Office theme" claim is FALSE; the test `w5_d_14_2_update_original_round_trip_preserves_opaque_theme` passes only because it asserts merely that `xl/theme/*` exists — not that the content matches.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:21:- What's wrong: `xl/worksheets/_rels/sheetN.xml.rels` and `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels` are NOT in `preserve_prefixes` and don't match any special-case. classify_part falls through to `PartAction::DropSilently`. Shadow's versions ALWAYS win (they're in `shadow_part_names`). Result: when the original has `<drawing r:id="rId4"/>` in its sheet rels (linking `xl/drawings/drawing1.xml`), we preserve `xl/drawings/drawing1.xml` (preserve_prefixes match) but drop the rels entry pointing to it. The drawing part becomes orphaned — Excel will silently strip on next save; LibreOffice may complain about a stale package.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:27:- What's wrong: `preserve_prefixes` includes `"xl/connections/"`, `"xl/customProperty/"`, `"xl/cellMetadata/"` (trailing slash, directory-form). But the real OOXML paths are single XML files: `xl/connections.xml`, `xl/customProperty.xml`, `xl/cellMetadata.xml`. `"xl/connections.xml".starts_with("xl/connections/")` is **false**. So these three part types match no preserve prefix, fall through to `DropSilently`, and are LOST without a `dropped_features` entry.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:28:- Why it matters: workbooks using Power Query, External Data Connections, or cell-metadata features (e.g. SpilledChartData) lose those features silently in UpdateOriginal. Users get no error, no report entry, and the original-side feature_inventory may have flagged them on import but the export-side silent-drop is invisible.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:34:- Why it matters: I ran 8 threads exporting to the same `/tmp/probe-corruption.xlsx` (Barrier-synced for max collision). Across 5 runs, **5-6 of 8 threads received WRONG output** every time. Each thread wrote a unique numeric sentinel to a unique column; on re-import, the sentinel was replaced with text/Blank values from a different thread's preservation source (basic_text.xlsx's shared-string content). This is silent data corruption: no error returned, output file looks valid, but cells contain another thread's content. The ScopedFileGuard then races on cleanup — `remove_file` of a nonexistent file is silently ignored.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:39:- What's wrong: Same root cause as H-2 at workbook level. The shadow's `xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels` only contains rels for the parts shadow emits (sheets, styles, theme, sharedStrings). The original's may contain additional rels for `pivotCache`, `connections`, `externalLinks`, `customXml`, `vbaProject`, etc. Original's workbook.rels file is named the same as shadow's → DropSilently. Original's rels are LOST.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:40:- Why it matters: even with H-1 fixed (preserved-prefix parts survive), the workbook-level Relationship entries that BIND them to the document are gone. The merged Content_Types may still have Overrides for the preserved parts, but Excel won't load them because there's no `r:id` linkage from `xl/workbook.xml/<extLst>` or similar. Net effect: pivot tables, external links, and custom XML mappings are silently broken even when the XML parts survive.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:50:- Why it matters: in v1 NewWorkbook mode, umya never emits any of these three elements pre-injection, so Case 1 never fires — empirically safe. But it's a latent corruption bomb: any future refactor that has umya emit `<numFmts>`/`<definedNames>`/`<tableParts>` (e.g., adopting a newer umya version that handles custom formats natively, or extending to UpdateOriginal with sheet-xml surgery) will silently produce invalid xlsx files.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:55:- What's wrong: needles are `<c r="C5" t="str"` and `<c r="C5" t="e"><v>#VALUE!</v>`. umya's cell writer (`umya-spreadsheet/src/structs/cell.rs:464-479`) emits attributes in order `r`, `t`, `s` — and emits `s="N"` for any cell where `stylesheet.set_style(...)` returns a non-zero xfId. For a styled error cell, umya writes `<c r="C5" t="e" s="2"><v>#VALUE!</v></c>`. The patch needle doesn't match; the cell silently keeps the umya hardcoded `#VALUE!` regardless of the actual error variant.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:56:- Why it matters: in v1, Quantbook's `apply_value_to_cell` doesn't apply per-cell styles (all error cells get default style 0), so empirically the patch matches. But the moment per-cell style application lands (W5-D-14 followups + Phase 4.12), styled error cells will silently corrupt to `#VALUE!` on export. Same defect applies to the `t="str"` removal.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:59:### M-3: Sheet-rels file is dropped silently when original has it but shadow has tables (overwriting original's drawing/comment rels)
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:68:- Why it matters: Excel allows `'` in sheet names (escaped as `''`). The fallback path captures the raw text as `Formula(...)`, which the binder MAY resolve later (Phase 3+). But until the binder lands, names targeting `O'Brien!$A$1` are effectively orphaned (no Cell/Range resolution). The export side handles the escape correctly (`quote_sheet_name` does `name.replace('\'', "''")`); only the import side is asymmetric.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:71:### M-5: Names that fail to register on import (reserved-name, unknown sheet for sheet-scoped, set_name error) are silently dropped even in Strict policy

Returns only the count of successfully-registered names. The caller (`lib.rs:184`) discards even that count (`let _names_registered = ...`). `UnsupportedPolicy::Strict` (in `lib.rs:189-208`) only fires for `feature_inventory.is_clean()` and doesn't include named-import failures. Strict mode is supposed to be the safety valve for round-trip correctness; this gap means a Strict import can return success while silently losing defined names.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:79:- What's wrong: classify_part returns `DropSilently` for `xl/calcChain.xml`, so `preserved_part_paths` doesn't include it. The merge logic at line 303 (`if !preserved_set.contains(normalised.as_str()) { continue; }`) skips it correctly. **No defect today.** Flagging because the design conflates "preserved" with "Content_Types-merged" — future divergence (e.g. someone adds a part that needs DropSilently but its Override should still be carried) requires both lists.

quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-array-formulas-and-spills.md:86:All rows must have the same number of cells. Mismatched-row literals (e.g. `{1, 2; 3}`) error at parse time with `ParseError::ArrayRowArityMismatch { expected, found, row }`. **This is a Quantbook v1 subset** — Excel pads with `#N/A` for missing cells, and `{1,2;3}` evaluates as `{1,2;3,#N/A}`. Quantbook v1 chooses loud rejection over silent padding; the pad-with-`#N/A` variant is a Phase 4.10 polish item gated on test-corpus completeness.
quantbook-engine/docs/architecture/2026-05-14-array-formulas-and-spills.md:645:`Workbook::register_spill` returns `Result<(), SpillBlockError>`. Runtime pre-validates + maps to `RuntimeError::Spill`. No silent failures. Pattern matches W5-93 sheet-name validation.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-5c-opus.md:56:#### M1. Silent rule-drop when column rename op's `table` field is stale relative to table's post-replay canonical
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-5c-opus.md:62:After `repair_table_rename_chain` rewrites `Tbl[A]` → `Sales[A]`, the column-repair pass tries to apply rule keyed by `("TBL", "a") → "AA"`. Since `current_columns_per_table` only has key `"SALES"` (post-replay canonical), the lookup fails and the rule is **silently dropped**. No entry in `ambiguous_rules_skipped` — silent formula corruption with no diagnostic surface.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-5c-opus.md:64:The docstring at `repair.rs:678-685` acknowledges this as "silently dropped (V1 limitation)" and dismisses it as "adversarial cross-peer interleavings." **My probe shows it's NOT adversarial**: a single log with the natural ordering (col rename → table rename → formula) triggers it. A 2-peer scenario where peer A col-renames then merges peer B's later table-rename is also natural, not adversarial.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7425:quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7454:quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:177:| SIN / COS / TAN / ASIN / ACOS / ATAN / ATAN2 | ✅ | 13 | 4.3 V2 | W5-51; ATAN2 uses Excel `(x, y)` arg order (not Rust's `(y, x)`); ATAN2(0,0)→#DIV/0!; ASIN/ACOS domain `|x|>1`→#NUM!; TAN(π/2) returns huge-finite (Excel canon, not error). **W5-D-13.1 megaudit closure (Codex HIGH-002 / Opus HIGH-2):** ATAN2 was previously unreachable from formula source (`ATAN2(1,1)` lex-errored with `ColumnTooLarge("ATAN")` — 4-letter prefix exceeded the 3-letter column-ref limit). The W5-D-13.1 lexer letters>3+digit Ident-fallback now emits `Ident("ATAN2")` so the parser dispatches correctly. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7455:quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:191:| SUMX2MY2 / SUMX2PY2 / SUMXMY2 | ✅ | 9 | 4.10.D | W5-166: paired array sum-of-squares variants. RangeAwareFn; both args must be ranges; W5-60 strict 2D-shape check (shape mismatch → #VALUE!). Non-numeric cells coerce to 0 (lenient, matches IronCalc canon). Errors in either array propagate. **W5-D-13.1 megaudit closure (Codex HIGH-002 / Opus HIGH-2):** SUMXMY2 was previously unreachable from formula source (`SUMXMY2(...)` lex-errored with `ColumnTooLarge("SUMXMY")`). The W5-D-13.1 lexer letters>3+digit Ident-fallback fixed it. SUMX2MY2 / SUMX2PY2 were already reachable via the W5-D-9 letters-digits-letters extension. Also admitted to `is_aggregate_function` in W5-D-13.1 for named-range arg support. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7460:quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:234:| DAYS / DAYS360 / NETWORKDAYS / NETWORKDAYS.INTL | ⚠️ | (see DATE row) | 4.5 V2 (W5-75) | W5-D-13.1: DAYS, DAYS360, NETWORKDAYS registered. **NETWORKDAYS.INTL not registered** (locale-aware variant — defer). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7472:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:50:- Why it matters: in v1 NewWorkbook mode, umya never emits any of these three elements pre-injection, so Case 1 never fires — empirically safe. But it's a latent corruption bomb: any future refactor that has umya emit `<numFmts>`/`<definedNames>`/`<tableParts>` (e.g., adopting a newer umya version that handles custom formats natively, or extending to UpdateOriginal with sheet-xml surgery) will silently produce invalid xlsx files.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7473:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:56:- Why it matters: in v1, Quantbook's `apply_value_to_cell` doesn't apply per-cell styles (all error cells get default style 0), so empirically the patch matches. Also admitted to `is_aggregate_function` in W5-D-13.1 for named-range arg support. |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:9095:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:2094:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:12:For W5-D-14, choose a round-trip spine rather than minimal import or read-only-full. The first batch should prove this vertical loop: import common cells/formulas/cached values, recover date system and scoped names from OOXML, detect styles/tables/CF/DV even if not all are implemented, recompute through `WorkbookRuntime`, and export a minimal/generated workbook or update formula caches in the original workbook with a visible report. This catches write-side integration bugs early while avoiding a false sense of safety from an importer that silently drops the very metadata Phase 4.11 says must survive where supported.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:9998:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:612:docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-2-opus.md:50:- Why it matters: in v1 NewWorkbook mode, umya never emits any of these three elements pre-injection, so Case 1 never fires — empirically safe. But it's a latent corruption bomb: any future refactor that has umya emit `<numFmts>`/`<definedNames>`/`<tableParts>` (e.g., adopting a newer umya version that handles custom formats natively, or extending to UpdateOriginal with sheet-xml surgery) will silently produce invalid xlsx files.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:10119:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-self.md:88:Note: W5-D-14b commit message accurately notes "scoped names PARSED but not yet registered with the engine NameTable (W5-D-15)". quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:10174:./quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:12:For W5-D-14, choose a round-trip spine rather than minimal import or read-only-full. The first batch should prove this vertical loop: import common cells/formulas/cached values, recover date system and scoped names from OOXML, detect styles/tables/CF/DV even if not all are implemented, recompute through `WorkbookRuntime`, and export a minimal/generated workbook or update formula caches in the original workbook with a visible report. This catches write-side integration bugs early while avoiding a false sense of safety from an importer that silently drops the very metadata Phase 4.11 says must survive where supported.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v4-v1-step-2-opus.md:27:- `pending_op_count`'s docstring justifies `saturating_sub` with "Loro's op log is append-only today, so the subtraction never actually underflows today." That is **false**. Undo retracts → `log.len()` decreases. If a successful flush set `last_flushed_op_count = Some(5)` and a subsequent undo (without a follow-up flush) drops `log.len()` to 4, the saturating subtraction silently masks underflow.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v4-v1-step-2-opus.md:64:**Gap:** none of the 6 new tests construct via `CollabSession::from_snapshot`. `from_snapshot` is used elsewhere in `auto_flush.rs` (lines 67, 148, 152, 351, 355, 632, 639, 686, 690, 1282, 1286) but none of those exercise `pending_op_count`. The docstring claim is unpinned — if a future refactor changes `from_snapshot` to initialize `last_flushed_op_count = Some(0)` "as a baseline," the claim silently becomes false and no test catches it.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v4-v1-step-2-opus.md:90:Under the H1 scenario (flush + undo without follow-up flush), `pending_op_count() == 0` while `has_pending_flush() == true`. The two observables disagree. The IDE wiring `if pending_op_count() > 0 { show_unsynced() }` will silently MISS the undo-pending state — exactly the kind of "Synced!" lie this gotcha section is supposed to prevent.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v4-v1-step-2-opus.md:104:`pending_op_count_grows_with_appends_pre_flush` asserts `>= 1` after one append and `>= 3` after three. If Loro silently counts container-init ops, the actual counts could be 1+K, 3+K for some constant K. Using `>=` lets the test pass for any K. A bug that double-counts (e.g., 2× per append → 2, 6) would still pass `>=`.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-5-opus.md:129:The anchor `0.715_356_905_970_664_3` is statrs's Newton-Raphson output for `t(0.975, df=9) / √10`. True math gives ≈ `0.71531056`. The test comment correctly documents this divergence and the test name `_statrs_self_consistent` reflects the W5-D-3 self-consistency pattern, so this is intentional. The LOW is only a flag: if statrs ever revises its inverse_cdf algorithm (e.g., higher-order Newton or analytic improvement), this anchor will silently shift and the test will fail. There's no test currently asserting "statrs's t(0.975, df=9) ≈ 2.262" as a checkpoint — only the composite `t·σ/√n` value is pinned. A second test pinning just `students_t_with(9.0).inverse_cdf(0.975)` (or referencing the existing T.INV test for this value) would localize a future statrs algorithm change to its source. Minor — current pattern is consistent with W5-D-3.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:9:W5-D-7 ships 2 RangeAwareFns closing the Wave-3-tagged matrix gap: `XNPV` (closed-form date-indexed NPV) and `XIRR` (date-indexed IRR via Newton-Raphson with bisection fallback). The diff is exactly the 5 files in the brief (financial_fns.rs, registry.rs, coverage.rs, region_mul2_e2e.rs, excel-matrix.md). 23 unit tests in the W5-D-7 block (11 XNPV + 12 XIRR) plus 1 e2e smoke pass. All 4 gates green (`cargo test --workspace` → 3767 passing; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo fmt --all --check` silent; coverage assertion 238). Registry size assertion bumped 236 → 238 and passes.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:27:- Newton-from-200 fallback: same 100-iter cap → bounded.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:42:| guess = NaN | converges via bisection fallback (Newton fails; bisect succeeds) |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:50:Findings: **0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 5 LOW**. Both MEDIUMs are IronCalc-parity divergences that the implementing instance flagged in code but the matrix-doc/test fixtures pin as the v1 behavior. Pattern prediction (1-2H for iterative kernel) does NOT hold — the iterative kernel is well-bounded by both 100-iter and 50-iter caps and a finite-check Err short-circuit. This is a tighter implementation than W5-D-4's BINOM.INV / W5-D-5's GAMMA.INV iterative kernels (which produced Codex HIGHs); the XIRR fallback ladder (Newton-from-guess → bisection → Newton-from-200) is more defensive than either.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:116:**Where**: `compute_xirr:1554-1564` — `for _ in 1..max_iterations { ... }` with `max_iterations = 50` runs 49 iterations, not 50. The pub doc on `xirr` says "Newton-Raphson on `XNPV(r) = 0` from `guess`; bisection fallback on `[-0.9999, 100]`" — doesn't specify count, so no drift there. The inline comment in `compute_xirr` doesn't claim 50 explicitly either. Just an off-by-one that mirrors IronCalc verbatim (`base/src/functions/financial_util.rs:242` uses the same `1..max_iterations`).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:120:### LOW-O-3 — `xirr` with `guess = NaN` silently converges via bisection
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:122:**Where**: `compute_xirr:1525` — `if guess <= -1.0 { return Err(Value) }`. NaN comparisons evaluate to `false`, so `NaN <= -1.0 == false` and NaN passes the guard. `xirr_newton(values, dates, NaN)` then computes `compute_xnpv(NaN, ...)` which produces NaN, fails the finite-check, returns `Err(Num)`; bisection fallback then runs with the original `values`/`dates` (NOT using guess) and succeeds.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:171:- **All gates pass**: `cargo fmt --all --check` silent; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean (only `Checking` and `Finished` lines); `cargo test --workspace` → 3767 passing.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:178:The iterative kernel is the cleanest of the Wave 3 iterative paths (W5-D-4 BINOM.INV and W5-D-5 GAMMA.INV both produced Codex HIGHs around iteration bounds). XIRR's three-layer fallback ladder (Newton-from-guess → bisection → Newton-from-200) is bounded on every layer, and the `is_finite()` short-circuit makes adversarial paths exit early rather than chase NaN/inf around the function space. The added `f_prime == 0` guard in `xirr_newton` is a strict improvement over IronCalc.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-codex.md:9:- **Detail:** `xirr_newton` accepts convergence solely when `abs(new_xirr - xirr) < 1e-7`, without checking the XNPV residual. Near the singularity at `rate = -1`, the Newton step can be tiny even while the residual is enormous. Repro at the kernel level: `values=[-100, 1000]`, `dates=[40000, 40365]`, `guess=-0.999999999`. The true one-year root is exactly `9.0` because `-100 + 1000/(1+r) = 0`; the first Newton step returns about `-0.999999998` because the step is only about `1e-9`, and `compute_xnpv` at that returned rate is still about `5e11`, not zero. Since `compute_xirr` immediately trusts `Ok(r)` from Newton, the bisection fallback is bypassed.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-codex.md:35:- **Subject:** XIRR fallback paths are not directly tested
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-codex.md:37:- **Detail:** The 12 new XIRR tests cover the canonical anchor, round-trip, sign validation, optional guess, empty/text semantics, length/date-order checks, error propagation, and arity. None force Newton to fail and then prove the bisection path on `[-0.9999, 100]` works, and none exercise the final `guess=200` Newton probe for roots above `100`. This is a gap relative to the risk profile of this batch and to the existing IRR test `irr_bisection_fallback_when_newton_diverges`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-codex.md:39:- **Severity rationale:** Low because the implementation paths exist and the loop bounds prevent hangs, but future edits could break fallback behavior while the current suite remains green.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-2-codex.md:7075:The intentional policy answers the CRDT case, but it also silently accepts single-writer malformed logs like `old="Wrong", new="X"` against current `S`, renaming `S -> X`. Replay currently cannot distinguish CRDT-merged vs single-writer from `OpLog::iter()`; it only sees `Op`. Suggested fix: update the public op docs and either bless advisory semantics everywhere or add an explicit strict replay mode / per-op causal metadata later. `let _ = old_name` is redundant because `old_name` is used in the rejection error closure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-2-codex.md:7098:Worst case: the HIGH remains an unrecoverable merged-log replay failure. The advisory `old_name` relaxation can become silent sheet-name corruption for malformed/snapshot-divergent single-writer logs.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v4-v1-step-4-opus.md:34:This is the SAME spawn → sync-lock → push pattern as `EchoServer::start`. Step 4 added the LOAD-BEARING comment ONLY on `EchoServer`. A future refactorer migrating one to `tokio::sync::Mutex` would read the EchoServer comment, NOT find the TextFrameServer site flagged, and silently introduce the documented leak. The K3 closure rationale (V2 V3 step 5 Opus-B M5) applies identically to TextFrameServer.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v4-v1-step-4-opus.md:38:Severity MEDIUM (not HIGH) because the only consumer is test code and the leak would manifest as a test-suite hang on the FIRST run, not a production bug. But it IS exactly the silent-migration risk the K3 comment exists to prevent.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2143:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:93:`crates/ql-functions/src/range_fns.rs:1386-1394`. CONCAT flattens by iterating the `values` Vec in its natural order. The shape comes from `env.read_range_with_shape` at `crates/ql-exec/src/env.rs:144-189`, which populates `for row { for col { out.push(...) } }` — row-major (left-to-right within a row, then row-by-row). For `A1:B2` the order is `A1, B1, A2, B2`. **This matches Excel's CONCAT canon.** But the doc comment on line 1374 just says "row-major order" without explaining what that means for a 2D range. The test `concat_flattens_range` (line 2644) uses a 1×N range, so it doesn't exercise the 2D semantics. A future contributor refactoring `read_range_with_shape` could silently flip this to column-major and only smoke tests on real sheets would catch it.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2324:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-5-opus.md:129:The anchor `0.715_356_905_970_664_3` is statrs's Newton-Raphson output for `t(0.975, df=9) / √10`. True math gives ≈ `0.71531056`. The test comment correctly documents this divergence and the test name `_statrs_self_consistent` reflects the W5-D-3 self-consistency pattern, so this is intentional. The LOW is only a flag: if statrs ever revises its inverse_cdf algorithm (e.g., higher-order Newton or analytic improvement), this anchor will silently shift and the test will fail. There's no test currently asserting "statrs's t(0.975, df=9) ≈ 2.262" as a checkpoint — only the composite `t·σ/√n` value is pinned. A second test pinning just `students_t_with(9.0).inverse_cdf(0.975)` (or referencing the existing T.INV test for this value) would localize a future statrs algorithm change to its source. Minor — current pattern is consistent with W5-D-3.
