quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2460:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:712:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:57:**Severity rationale:** No correctness bug — the behavior is correct under the current code path. But the missing pins mean a future refactor could silently change behavior without test failure. NaN-k in particular: a refactor that moves the bound check below the `pos.floor() as usize` cast (which is `0` for NaN, not a panic in safe-cast Rust) would silently return `sorted[0]` instead of `#NUM!` — a real correctness regression that would slip through.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2461:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:713:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:65:**Detail:** Per Codex's documentation review (citing Microsoft TRUNC + QUARTILE.INC docs), Excel truncates a fractional `quart` argument toward zero (TRUNC, not FLOOR). The current implementation uses `n.trunc() as i64` — **correct per Microsoft canon**. But the test suite only pins the positive-fractional case (`quartile_inc_q_truncates_toward_zero`: 2.9 → 2). The negative-fractional case (e.g. `quartile_inc(arr, -0.5)` should return the minimum, NOT `#NUM!`) is NOT pinned. A naive future refactor to `n.floor() as i64` (a plausible misreading of "truncated") would silently change behavior on a sliver of input space without test failure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2467:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:721:docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:37:The doc also needs explicit rejection behavior for mixed-sheet two-endpoint ranges such as `Sheet1!A1:Sheet2!B2` and future 3D ranges such as `Sheet1:Sheet3!A1`. Without this, implementers may accidentally create same-sheet fallbacks or silently normalize invalid cross-sheet ranges.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2487:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:744:docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-closing-megaudit-codex.md:2560:./docs/audits/2026-05-15-phase-4.9-design-review-codex.md:338:   153	6. **Persistence: forward-compat for locales** — if a future v8 adds `LocaleId::Ja`, current v7 reader sees an unknown locale string and... rejects? Falls back to En? Per CLAUDE.md "no fallbacks" — rejects loud.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2528:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:805:docs/audits/2026-05-13-session-final-megaudit-codex.txt:1149:The W5-50 → W5-52 arc is the case study. W5-50 shipped under "GAP-G-01 closed" framing. The `on_clear_formula` clear-path bug shipped silently. W5-52 mega-audit (Codex + Sonnet) caught it because both auditors independently flagged the same staleness class on the clear path. Without the parallel pattern, a future regression in this surface would have been the first time the bug surfaced — much later, in user code.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2550:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:854:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2552:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:856:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2555:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:859:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:379:The four MEDIUM findings are all latent (no current crash or data-loss in the happy path) and address areas where the implementation silently diverges from the design doc or creates footguns for future contributors. The four LOW findings are test-infrastructure and documentation gaps. The overall implementation quality is high: the core parser-workbook decoupling, two-tier name chain, schema v5 save/load, replay reconciliation, and formula-text rewrite on rename are all correctly implemented.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2568:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:877:docs/audits/2026-05-13-finalization-planning-codex.txt:3062:   152	However, as noted in the brief: Phase 3.3 sets `range.sheet = Some(_)` always during binding, so the `unwrap_or(fs)` fallback is currently unreachable. The future cross-sheet case (Phase 4.6) will work correctly if the binder sets `sheet: Some(target_sheet)` for cross-sheet refs. The one risk: if a future binder sets `sheet: None` for cross-sheet refs and relies on context, the supplemental builder would incorrectly scope G's to F's sheet. This is a latent risk, not a current bug.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2575:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:885:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:211:**Severity rationale:** HIGH because (a) the plan checklist explicitly enumerated this coverage class; (b) the no-eval guarantee is the SINGLE most important contract for `ArgContract::LazyShape` (the design's HIGH-B closure); (c) the regression risk is high — a future materializer refactor that "for consistency" applies eager-eval to LazyShape args would silently break the contract; (d) the current `isref_of_divide_by_zero_returns_false_without_eval` test only catches the case where eval would surface an error — it does NOT catch the case where eval succeeds but writes to the cache or fires side effects. This is the same pattern as Step 1's HIGH-O-1 (doc-promised invariant test missing).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2576:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:886:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:256:### MEDIUM-S3-O-1 — `step_2_reference_aware_names_registered_in_reference_tier` disjointness check missing `lookup_context_aware`. The test pinpoints ISREF / ISFORMULA must NOT appear in scalar / range-aware / unified tables, but skips the context-aware tier. A future typo registering ISREF as `register_context_aware` would silently slip through.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2577:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:889:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:311:1. **Semantic divergence.** Under the design's pseudo-code, `RefArg::Error(_)` would fall through `_ => Value::Error(ErrorValue::NA)` (arity error). The impl returns `Value::Boolean(false)`. These are different user-visible results. Even though the impl path is "unreachable under LazyShape contract", **someone might invoke `isref()` directly from a future test or extension**, and the behavior would silently differ from spec.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3340:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:537:docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:93:`crates/ql-functions/src/range_fns.rs:1386-1394`. CONCAT flattens by iterating the `values` Vec in its natural order. The shape comes from `env.read_range_with_shape` at `crates/ql-exec/src/env.rs:144-189`, which populates `for row { for col { out.push(...) } }` — row-major (left-to-right within a row, then row-by-row). For `A1:B2` the order is `A1, B1, A2, B2`. **This matches Excel's CONCAT canon.** But the doc comment on line 1374 just says "row-major order" without explaining what that means for a 2D range. The test `concat_flattens_range` (line 2644) uses a 1×N range, so it doesn't exercise the 2D semantics. A future contributor refactoring `read_range_with_shape` could silently flip this to column-major and only smoke tests on real sheets would catch it.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3629:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1061:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-sonnet-review.md:110:The register loop computes `MAX_ROW + 1` as `u32` — no overflow (MAX_ROW = 1_048_575, u32::MAX = 4_294_967_295) — but it inserts a target entry for a logically out-of-bounds row. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:4356:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-5-opus.md:129:The anchor `0.715_356_905_970_664_3` is statrs's Newton-Raphson output for `t(0.975, df=9) / √10`. A second test pinning just `students_t_with(9.0).inverse_cdf(0.975)` (or referencing the existing T.INV test for this value) would localize a future statrs algorithm change to its source. Minor — current pattern is consistent with W5-D-3.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:4535:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:169:**Files:** `crates/ql-formula-syntax/tests/p412_defensive_fuzz_probes.rs` — the `try_parse` wrapper uses `panic::catch_unwind` but doesn't isolate to a separate thread. When `deep_function_call_1000` overflows the test-binary main-thread stack, the whole binary aborts — no assertion ever runs, and all subsequent tests in the file silently skip. Engineering note for future fuzz work: every recursion probe must run inside a `thread::Builder::default().spawn(...)` so the overflow is contained.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:5310:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-opus.md:244:The "populated when the consumer iterates" promise is **not implemented** — there's no path that populates `values`. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-audit-summary.md:172:1. **Coverage gaps tend to slip when test infrastructure differs.** Named-range / cross-sheet / structured-ref / formula-cell-context each require non-trivial test setup (NameTable / sheet resolver / WorkbookRuntime). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.C-sonnet-review.md:141:**How this manifests:** A new `ErrorValue::Foo` added to `sigil()` but not `ALL` would compile, pass all existing tests, and silently reject `#FOO!` as `InvalidErrorSigil` in the lexer.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:869:quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

But the missing pins mean a future refactor could silently change behavior without test failure. NaN-k in particular: a refactor that moves the bound check below the `pos.floor() as usize` cast (which is `0` for NaN, not a panic in safe-cast Rust) would silently return `sorted[0]` instead of `#NUM!` — a real correctness regression that would slip through.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:940:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2461:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:713:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:65:**Detail:** Per Codex's documentation review (citing Microsoft TRUNC + QUARTILE.INC docs), Excel truncates a fractional `quart` argument toward zero (TRUNC, not FLOOR). The current implementation uses `n.trunc() as i64` — **correct per Microsoft canon**. But the test suite only pins the positive-fractional case (`quartile_inc_q_truncates_toward_zero`: 2.9 → 2). The negative-fractional case (e.g. `quartile_inc(arr, -0.5)` should return the minimum, NOT `#NUM!`) is NOT pinned. A naive future refactor to `n.floor() as i64` (a plausible misreading of "truncated") would silently change behavior on a sliver of input space without test failure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:950:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:2592:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:906:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:94:**Impact:** Behavioral inconsistency with the port source (IronCalc) **on the most-used arg type** (Boolean in numeric position). When IronCalc fixtures are eventually built to cross-check NORM.* — which is the natural next step for Wave 3 cohort-wide regression testing — they will diverge silently OR force re-port. Catching the divergence in documentation NOW means the future fixture-author knows where to expect deltas.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:986:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3400:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:713:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:65:**Detail:** Per Codex's documentation review (citing Microsoft TRUNC + QUARTILE.INC docs), Excel truncates a fractional `quart` argument toward zero (TRUNC, not FLOOR). The current implementation uses `n.trunc() as i64` — **correct per Microsoft canon**. But the test suite only pins the positive-fractional case (`quartile_inc_q_truncates_toward_zero`: 2.9 → 2). The negative-fractional case (e.g. `quartile_inc(arr, -0.5)` should return the minimum, NOT `#NUM!`) is NOT pinned. A naive future refactor to `n.floor() as i64` (a plausible misreading of "truncated") would silently change behavior on a sliver of input space without test failure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:996:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3531:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:906:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-1-opus.md:94:**Impact:** Behavioral inconsistency with the port source (IronCalc) **on the most-used arg type** (Boolean in numeric position). When IronCalc fixtures are eventually built to cross-check NORM.* — which is the natural next step for Wave 3 cohort-wide regression testing — they will diverge silently OR force re-port. Catching the divergence in documentation NOW means the future fixture-author knows where to expect deltas.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1010:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-4-v1-codex.md:3632:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1064:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:104:- **Detail:** Both engine `scalar_fns::counta` and IronCalc `subtotal_counta` count errors (engine: `!matches!(v, Value::Blank).count()` includes Error; IronCalc: `String | Number | Boolean | Error => counta += 1`). Behavior matches. **However**, this is NOT pinned by any SUBTOTAL test — the `subtotal_counta_function_num_3` test only covers `[1, "skip", 2, blank, 3]` (no error). A future refactor of `scalar_fns::counta` to skip errors would silently break compatibility with IronCalc + Excel canon (Excel COUNTA does count errors) and the engine-wide aggregate convention. Probe-verified: `SUBTOTAL(3, [1, #DIV/0!, 3]) = ?`. **Not tested** in the new SUBTOTAL block (probe-confirmed = 3.0 — passes through to counta which counts the error).

The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). The W5-D-13.1 lexer letters>3+digit Ident-fallback now emits `Ident("ATAN2")` so the parser dispatches correctly. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1475:quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:191:| SUMX2MY2 / SUMX2PY2 / SUMXMY2 | ✅ | 9 | 4.10.D | W5-166: paired array sum-of-squares variants. RangeAwareFn; both args must be ranges; W5-60 strict 2D-shape check (shape mismatch → #VALUE!). Non-numeric cells coerce to 0 (lenient, matches IronCalc canon). Errors in either array propagate. **W5-D-13.1 megaudit closure (Codex HIGH-002 / Opus HIGH-2):** SUMXMY2 was previously unreachable from formula source (`SUMXMY2(...)` lex-errored with `ColumnTooLarge("SUMXMY")`). The W5-D-13.1 lexer letters>3+digit Ident-fallback fixed it. SUMX2MY2 / SUMX2PY2 were already reachable via the W5-D-9 letters-digits-letters extension. Also admitted to `is_aggregate_function` in W5-D-13.1 for named-range arg support. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1480:quantbook-engine/docs/compat/excel-matrix.md:234:| DAYS / DAYS360 / NETWORKDAYS / NETWORKDAYS.INTL | ⚠️ | (see DATE row) | 4.5 V2 (W5-75) | W5-D-13.1: DAYS, DAYS360, NETWORKDAYS registered. **NETWORKDAYS.INTL not registered** (locale-aware variant — defer). DAYS360 was previously also blocked at lex time (4-letter prefix); W5-D-13.1 lexer Ident-fallback closure makes it reachable from source text. |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1518:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-self.md:41:**Severity rationale:** Real bind-time correctness bug. 28 user-facing fns silently broken for named-range usage. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1520:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-self.md:145:**Severity rationale:** Not a current correctness bug (sanitize_f64 catches NaN upstream). But MEDIUM because (a) the defensive pattern is inconsistent across Phase 4.10 — some places have explicit guards, others rely on implicit upstream behavior; (b) a future refactor could silently break it; (c) the W5-D-12.1 closure documented this as a forward-lesson but didn't retroactively apply it.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1594:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-opus.md:660:| `styles_xml.rs:180` | `num_fmt_id = val.parse::<u32>().unwrap_or(0)` | LOAD-BEARING: silently maps malformed numFmtId to General (FormatId 0) |
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:1624:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-codex.txt:7357:    80	| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:2094:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:12:For W5-D-14, choose a round-trip spine rather than minimal import or read-only-full. The first batch should prove this vertical loop: import common cells/formulas/cached values, recover date system and scoped names from OOXML, detect styles/tables/CF/DV even if not all are implemented, recompute through `WorkbookRuntime`, and export a minimal/generated workbook or update formula caches in the original workbook with a visible report. This catches write-side integration bugs early while avoiding a false sense of safety from an importer that silently drops the very metadata Phase 4.11 says must survive where supported.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-22-phase-5-7-v1-megaudit-codex.md:5527:   210	- **Offline-write (✅ Phase 5.5 V2 V3 step 3 SHIPPED 2026-05-21)**: append while no transport attached → `append_op` returns `Ok(())` and commits locally; `maybe_auto_flush` silently no-ops. **Loro's CRDT op log IS the implicit offline queue — no separate buffer needed.** On reattach: `attach_transport` resets `last_flushed_vv = None`. The next mutator (or explicit `flush_delta_to_transport`) sends the delta from empty VV — delivers ALL accumulated ops including the offline ones. Recovery from a failed flush (transport closed mid-session) follows the same pattern: the failed-flush op is committed locally; detach + reattach (or just reattach — it replaces + resets) + explicit flush sends everything. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-sonnet-review.md:110:The register loop computes `MAX_ROW + 1` as `u32` — no overflow (MAX_ROW = 1_048_575, u32::MAX = 4_294_967_295) — but it inserts a target entry for a logically out-of-bounds row. The storage layer silently accepts this. This is intentional per design, but a test documenting the behavior (even just asserting the registration succeeds and a target at `MAX_ROW+1` exists in the map) would lock in the "storage is bounds-agnostic" contract so a future reviewer doesn't add accidental defensive clamping.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-sonnet-review.md:156:**Double-clear scenario:** If a caller calls `Workbook::clear_computed_at(s, r, c)` on a cell that is a spill target, then later calls `clear_spill_at`, the inner loop calls `sheet.clear_computed(arow+dr, acol+dc)` on an already-cleared cell. `clear_computed` on a cell with no computed overlay is a no-op in the `ColumnStore`/`SparseOverlay` layer — BTreeMap remove on a missing key returns `None` silently. Idempotent, no issue.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-1-opus.md:27:**Why it matters**: A regression where `put_at` STARTS clearing formula_cells, or where the read cascade flips to prefer computed-overlay, or where one op silently no-ops, would all leave this test green while the property is broken. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:23:`Workbook::add_sheet` (`workbook.rs:463–473`) does NOT call `validate_sheet_name`. The storage-layer `add_sheet` method also lacks a `try_add_sheet` variant with name validation. Duplicate names can be silently created at the raw storage level:
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:27:wb.add_sheet("sheet1"); // silently creates a second sheet with canonical collision
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:62:The lexer only enters `try_lex_sheet_name_prefix` for `[A-Za-z_]`; digit-starting names (e.g., `1Sheet`) route to `lex_number`, leaving `!` as an unexpected token. This means digit-starting names MUST be quoted. No explicit rejection at lex time; the parse will surface an error via the unexpected `!`. The lexer does not silently accept malformed input — it surfaces errors at a different layer. This is consistent with Excel's behavior (digit-starting sheet names must always be quoted). Documenting rather than flagging.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:122:`plan.rs:474–478` — returns `None` for all sheets, which propagates to `UnknownSheet`. Correct fallback for name-only bind paths.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:131:**G.2 — Out-of-range `owning_sheet` fallback:** PASS  
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. This means a v6+ entry with an additional field in a `NamedEntry` object would be silently ignored rather than loudly rejected. The existing v1-v4 / v5 compatibility is unaffected, but the "strict forward-compat" invariant (established in Phase 2A.8 megaudit) is violated for this struct. Severity: LOW (only matters if a future schema version adds a `NamedEntry` field without bumping the version gate).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:277:`producer_replay_equivalence.rs:202–288`: the comparator checks: sheet count, sheet names, cell values, formula texts, `wb.names()` (workbook-scoped), `FormatTable`, and `CellFormatOverlay`. It does NOT check per-sheet `scoped_names`. A divergence in sheet-scoped names between producer and replay workbooks would pass this comparator silently. Severity: LOW (the replay unit tests cover the routing logic; this is a test-infrastructure gap).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:379:The four MEDIUM findings are all latent (no current crash or data-loss in the happy path) and address areas where the implementation silently diverges from the design doc or creates footguns for future contributors. The four LOW findings are test-infrastructure and documentation gaps. The overall implementation quality is high: the core parser-workbook decoupling, two-tier name chain, schema v5 save/load, replay reconciliation, and formula-text rewrite on rename are all correctly implemented.

State: `last_flushed_vv = None` (not advanced on Err per session.rs:941-944), `has_pending_flush() = true`, `has_transport() = true` (the attached WS is still attached even though it's dead — session doesn't auto-detach on send error). quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-5-codex.md:10986:Executive summary: VERDICT: FAIL. I found one HIGH in the V1-limitation re-verification: `DropTable × concurrent RenameTable` is not simply “hard-fails”; it is order-dependent. With drop before rename, replay succeeds and silently drops the rename intent; with rename before drop, replay hard-fails via `TableNotFound`. The rest of the 5.3 cross-step invariants are broadly intact, but there is doc rot around post-step-3/post-step-4 behavior, public 5.3 APIs are not yet in the IDE consumer contract, and the real formula-rewrite helper duplication count is 5 even though exact `ql_formula_syntax::lex` grep returns 3.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-5-codex.md:11028:Executive summary: VERDICT: FAIL. I found one HIGH in the V1-limitation re-verification: `DropTable × concurrent RenameTable` is not simply “hard-fails”; it is order-dependent. With drop before rename, replay succeeds and silently drops the rename intent; with rename before drop, replay hard-fails via `TableNotFound`. The rest of the 5.3 cross-step invariants are broadly intact, but there is doc rot around post-step-3/post-step-4 behavior, public 5.3 APIs are not yet in the IDE consumer contract, and the real formula-rewrite helper duplication count is 5 even though exact `ql_formula_syntax::lex` grep returns 3.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-5b-opus.md:23:2. **`sync_workbook` is non-idempotent and has no guard against the most obvious misuse paths.** Empirical probes show silent-corruption shapes for double-invocation, stale-workbook-from-other-log, and double-invocation-with-repair. The wrapper enforces the SEQUENCE (replay → repair) but not the PRECONDITION (clean / fresh workbook).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:10:Use `umya-spreadsheet` as the first writer backend for round-trip/update-original workflows, and keep the writer behind a backend boundary so a generated-workbook path can later use `rust_xlsxwriter` where appropriate. The important distinction is not cached formula values: current `rust_xlsxwriter` can store a formula result manually through `Formula::set_result()` / `Worksheet::set_formula_result()`. The real distinction is that `rust_xlsxwriter` is a strong generator, while Quantbook's first fidelity problem is preserving or updating an existing XLSX package without silently discarding user-owned workbook features.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:12:For W5-D-14, choose a round-trip spine rather than minimal import or read-only-full. The first batch should prove this vertical loop: import common cells/formulas/cached values, recover date system and scoped names from OOXML, detect styles/tables/CF/DV even if not all are implemented, recompute through `WorkbookRuntime`, and export a minimal/generated workbook or update formula caches in the original workbook with a visible report. This catches write-side integration bugs early while avoiding a false sense of safety from an importer that silently drops the very metadata Phase 4.11 says must survive where supported.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:31:`calamine` should own the common grid path: sheet names/order as seen by the reader, sparse cell values, formula ranges via `worksheet_formula`, and basic defined names only as fallback. This buys a battle-tested parser for shared strings, numbers, booleans, errors, formula cells, and sheet iteration. That is the fastest way to close XLSX-4-01 and to avoid spending the first week rediscovering ordinary worksheet parsing bugs.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:43:- Emit `XlsxImportReport` entries for every unsupported OOXML feature found. Silent drop should be a test failure for strict mode.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:55:Quantbook is not shaped that way. It has a semantic workbook and graph runtime, not an OOXML DOM. A roll-own first pass would still need all the same package parsing, then substantial glue to compress OOXML into Quantbook concepts. It would surface many basic bugs early, but it would also push the first recompute/export loop later and leave a long tail of OOXML conformance bugs owned by this repo. Roll-own should remain a fallback/migration path behind our own `GridReader` and `PackageScanner` traits, not the starting point.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:230:- `CalamineGridReader`: returns sheets, sparse values, formula strings, cached values, and raw calamine metadata fallback.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-architecture-codex.md:253:The key assertion is not that every OOXML feature is implemented in batch one. The key assertion is that Quantbook never silently claims fidelity it does not have.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-phase-2B.md:65:- `chunk_rows == 0`: accepted silently → sheet created with `chunk_rows=0` → first cell write panics in `ColumnStore::with_chunk_rows`. Op log persists the bad `Op::AddSheet`; replay reproduces the same poison on next load.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-phase-2B.md:75:The 2B.5 implementation chose mutate-first ordering to avoid orphan log entries on reserved-name rejection. But on an op-log append failure AFTER the workbook mutation, the workbook had the new name and the log didn't — silent divergence that would replay-corrupt on next load.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-phase-2B.md:93:The two-pass commit ran pass 1 (literals + formula text) and pass 2 (eval + write formula values) BEFORE appending the `Op::BatchCommit` to the log. A serialization failure on the append (e.g., NaN/Inf in a `Value::Number`) would leave the workbook fully mutated and the log without the entry. Save/load would lose the changes silently.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5183-vdb-audit-summary.md:45:- **HIGH-1**: `salvage > cost` silently returns 0. LibreOffice / OpenFormula reject with `#NUM!`. We didn't validate; our impl returns 0 because `book - salvage < 0` clamps DDB to 0 and the negative SLN check never switches.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-codex.md:52:1. **Advisory skip for tables (V1 limitation)**: when peer A renames T→T2 and peer B (concurrent) renames T→T3, peer B's intent is dropped silently. Is this DOCUMENTED clearly enough? Is there a regression risk where a future change makes the skip non-silent (e.g., a logging side-effect) that breaks the test?
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-codex.md:54:2. **`apply_rename_table` case (b)**: my current implementation silently `return Ok(())` for the "missing source, new_name also missing" case. This covers the "concurrent T→T2 vs T→T3" scenario (peer B's op replays after A's, current state has T2 not T, T3 doesn't exist yet). But what if a peer issues `RenameTable { "Wrong", "X" }` against a workbook that genuinely doesn't have Wrong or X? Pre-step-4 errored with `TableNotFound`; post-step-4 silently no-ops. Is this acceptable for the single-writer case? Could this hide bugs in producer-side validation?

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-codex.md:6190:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-1-codex.md:869:quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-codex.md:6287:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:606:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.F-codex-review.txt:6618:9. PASS with future-test requirement: The current cell-boundary interim state is sound because the spill path is explicitly deferred and `WorkbookRuntime::set_formula` still routes root formulas through scalar eval at `crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime.rs:524`. In 4.7.J, root array/spill detection must intercept before those eval calls; otherwise the failure mode is visible `#CALC!`, not silent scalar truncation. Add runtime tests for `={1,2}` at a cell root spilling rather than returning `#CALC!`.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-codex.md:6293:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:856:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). However, the formula text is persisted via `.qbook` save/load and op-log replay — a stale text will silently carry incorrect references into future phases when named formulas are evaluated. The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-codex.md:6689:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-2-d-1-step-2-codex.md:7425:quantbook-engine/docs/known-gaps.md:83:| GAP-F-12 | `WorkbookRuntime::format_cache` can stale if `Workbook::formats_mut()` mutates the FormatTable AFTER `read_display` has cached the General fallback for a (then-unknown) id. The cache is keyed by `FormatId`; cache entries stay correct as long as mutations go through `WorkbookRuntime::intern_format` (the documented append-before-mutate path). Direct low-level mutation through `formats_mut()` (loader / tests only) on a live runtime is the pathological sequence. Analogous to the `WorkbookEnv` date-system staleness caveat documented at `Workbook::set_date_system`. **Decision (W5-84):** documented in the `read_display` docstring; cache-invalidation API deferred until profiling shows a real-world hit. | Filed W5-84 mega-audit closure (Codex MEDIUM-2) | Engine | Engine Phase 4.10 polish or earlier if IDE forces it |

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-codex.md:8109:1. [repair.rs](/Users/sanzhar/Documents/Sanzhar/Sanzhar/quantlab/quantlab-quantbook/quantbook-engine/crates/ql-collab/src/repair.rs:394): table repair is wrong after table auto-disambiguation. `collect_table_renames` keys history by the op’s requested `new_name`, not the actual post-replay table name. For `T1 -> X` and `T3 -> X`, replay produces `{X, X(2)}`, but repair stores both historic names under `"X"`. Phase 3 then emits rules like `T3 -> X`, even when `T3` is the table that actually became `X(2)`. That can rewrite `T3[B]` to `X[B]`, causing `#NAME?` or silently reading the wrong table if columns overlap. This is worse than “misses the rewrite”; it can corrupt formulas.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-codex.md:8133:Step 4 fixes the immediate hard-fail class, but the repair extension is not sound once replay auto-disambiguates table names, and the column side has the same formula-corruption shape with no repair pass. The advisory skip itself is defensible as a V1 limitation, but the implementation currently makes corrupt single-writer rename ops silently disappear and the public docs/test coverage do not make that contract crisp. I would not ship this commit as closure without at least fixing table repair’s actual-name mapping for suffixes and either landing column repair or explicitly documenting/probing the column formula corruption limitation.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-opus.md:14:Step 4 ships the right algorithmic skeleton — replay no longer hard-fails, the chain-walk in `repair_table_rename_chain` mirrors the audit-locked sheet design, and the safety guard correctly extends step 3's closure to tables. However, **one HIGH (silent formula corruption when replay auto-disambiguates) is untested and reaches production**, and **the column repair gap is more severe than the step 4 commit messaging implies**.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-opus.md:16:## HIGH-1: Auto-disambiguated table repair silently corrupts formulas — repair maps to wrong table
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-opus.md:20:**What**: When replay auto-disambiguates (peer A: T1→X; peer B: T2→X → {X, X(2)}), the op log retains peer B's `new_name="X"`. `collect_table_renames` builds `historic_by_current[X] = [T1, T2]` because both ops nominally renamed-to-X. Peer B's formula `=T2[col]` (intending X(2)) is rewritten to `=X[col]` (the OTHER table). **Silent cross-table reference corruption.**
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-opus.md:52:**What**: Sheet case-only APPLIES; Table case-only SILENTLY NO-OPS; Column case-only HARD-REJECTS. Three different policies.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-opus.md:78:Step 4 successfully extends the step-2 RenameSheet algorithm to RenameTable/RenameColumn replay (advisory-skip + safety guard) and adds `repair_table_rename_chain`. The audit caught that the auto-disambig + repair interaction was silently corrupting formulas (HIGH-1) and that column repair was missing (HIGH-2). Both HIGHs closed by REVERTING auto-disambig and documenting the cross-source target collision as a V1 limitation. The four MEDIUM findings are split: M-2 closed (dead state removed), M-4 closed (test added), M-1 + M-3 deferred to step 5 megaudit. The pragmatic revert preserves step 4's primary closure (Opus step 1 audit M-2: rename hard-fail on missing source) while avoiding the silent-corruption HIGHs.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-codex.md:31:**Detail:** The design models ROWS/COLUMNS as reference-only. Excel and LibreOffice both define them over references and arrays. Microsoft examples include `ROWS({1,2,3;4,5,6}) = 2` and `COLUMNS({1,2,3;4,5,6}) = 3`; the current engine already has `FunctionArg::Array` for Unified functions (`registry.rs:63`). The proposed `RefArg` has no `Array` variant, and the materializer fallback would evaluate `ExprPlan::Array` in scalar context to `#CALC!`, then ROWS/COLUMNS would likely turn that into `#VALUE!`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-codex.md:57:### HIGH-6 — ROW/COLUMN spill defer would silently return the wrong result
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-codex.md:61:**Detail:** The design defers array-spilling ROW/COLUMN and says multi-cell ranges return the top-left index. That matches old scalar-context behavior, but the engine already has a cell-boundary spill path (`eval_at_cell_boundary`) and Microsoft 365 / LibreOffice array semantics for `ROW(A1:A5)` and `COLUMN(A1:C1)` return arrays. If the new tier only returns `Value`, top-level `=ROW(A1:A5)` will silently compute `1` instead of spilling `{1;2;3;4;5}` or at least surfacing an explicit unsupported-array error.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-codex.md:63:**Recommendation:** Either implement ROW/COLUMN as array-returning at the cell boundary for multi-row/multi-column references, or explicitly return `#CALC!` for multi-cell ROW/COLUMN until spill support is added. Do not silently top-left in dynamic-array contexts.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-design-codex.md:65:**Severity rationale:** Silent scalar truncation is likely incorrect output in modern Excel-compatible workbooks.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-codex-review.txt:44:3. The Workbook::clear_spill_at signature: returns SpillNotFoundError on miss. Callers (the future 4.7.J runtime path) will likely WANT idempotent clearing — call it whether or not the anchor exists, succeed silently. Should this be split into a `try_clear_spill_at` (errors) and `clear_spill_if_present` (idempotent)?
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-codex-review.txt:45:4. `clear_spill_at` iterates the rectangle using `arow + dr`, `acol + dc`. Same overflow concern as #2. If the runtime registered a spill that PRE-overflowed (caller mistake), unregister would silently miss cells.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-codex-review.txt:147:All rows must have the same number of cells. Mismatched-row literals (e.g. `{1, 2; 3}`) error at parse time with `ParseError::ArrayRowArityMismatch { expected, found, row }`. **This is a Quantbook v1 subset** — Excel pads with `#N/A` for missing cells, and `{1,2;3}` evaluates as `{1,2;3,#N/A}`. Quantbook v1 chooses loud rejection over silent padding; the pad-with-`#N/A` variant is a Phase 4.10 polish item gated on test-corpus completeness.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:78:- **Severity rationale:** Without an end-to-end test, the implementation could silently regress at the binder/dispatch level (e.g., a registration typo, an `is_aggregate_function` change that drops SUBTOTAL) and the unit tests would still pass. Other fns get away with this because their unit tests + the existing aggregate fns in the file collectively cover the binder path. SUBTOTAL is the first range-aware fn where the unit tests use `FnArg::Range` directly — a path that bypasses the binder entirely.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:104:- **Detail:** Both engine `scalar_fns::counta` and IronCalc `subtotal_counta` count errors (engine: `!matches!(v, Value::Blank).count()` includes Error; IronCalc: `String | Number | Boolean | Error => counta += 1`). Behavior matches. **However**, this is NOT pinned by any SUBTOTAL test — the `subtotal_counta_function_num_3` test only covers `[1, "skip", 2, blank, 3]` (no error). A future refactor of `scalar_fns::counta` to skip errors would silently break compatibility with IronCalc + Excel canon (Excel COUNTA does count errors) and the engine-wide aggregate convention. Probe-verified: `SUBTOTAL(3, [1, #DIV/0!, 3]) = ?`. **Not tested** in the new SUBTOTAL block (probe-confirmed = 3.0 — passes through to counta which counts the error).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-pre-review-summary.md:77:**HIGH-E — ROW / COLUMN multi-cell silent truncation at cell-boundary.** (Codex HIGH-6, Opus-implicit-via-LOW-5.)
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-pre-review-summary.md:79:In a top-level `=ROW(A1:A5)`, Excel 365 spills to `{1;2;3;4;5}`. The design's "top-left only" return would silently produce `1` even in cell-boundary array context, where `eval_at_cell_boundary` already supports spilling via the Unified tier.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-reference-tier-pre-review-summary.md:81:**Closure (v2):** Reference-tier fns called via `eval_at_cell_boundary` with a multi-cell `RefArg::Range` or `RefArg::Array` arg return `Value::Error(ErrorValue::Calc)` (`#CALC!`) instead of silently truncating. This matches the existing Unified-tier "array in scalar context → #CALC!" contract (W5-100 / scalar.rs:307-315). Spill-form ROW/COLUMN is a follow-up; this commit explicitly avoids silent wrong-results. Documented in v2 § 2.1, § 8 R5.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:512:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-5-opus.md:129:The anchor `0.715_356_905_970_664_3` is statrs's Newton-Raphson output for `t(0.975, df=9) / √10`. True math gives ≈ `0.71531056`. The test comment correctly documents this divergence and the test name `_statrs_self_consistent` reflects the W5-D-3 self-consistency pattern, so this is intentional. The LOW is only a flag: if statrs ever revises its inverse_cdf algorithm (e.g., higher-order Newton or analytic improvement), this anchor will silently shift and the test will fail. There's no test currently asserting "statrs's t(0.975, df=9) ≈ 2.262" as a checkpoint — only the composite `t·σ/√n` value is pinned. A second test pinning just `students_t_with(9.0).inverse_cdf(0.975)` (or referencing the existing T.INV test for this value) would localize a future statrs algorithm change to its source. Minor — current pattern is consistent with W5-D-3.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:518:docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-codex.txt:4870:         // behavior so a future change can't drift silently.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:536:docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:73:CONCERN-B in the audit brief specifically called these out. If the W5-61 commit prose claims "behavior-preserving rewrite", these are the exact contracts that need pinning to prevent a future refactor from silently regressing them. The W5-56 SEARCH ship may have had these tests; let me note that I greped `crates/ql-functions/src/scalar_fns.rs` for `search_empty\|search.*needle\|empty.*needle.*search` and got zero hits — neither the W5-56 ship nor W5-61 has them.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:537:docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-61-megaudit-sonnet.md:93:`crates/ql-functions/src/range_fns.rs:1386-1394`. CONCAT flattens by iterating the `values` Vec in its natural order. The shape comes from `env.read_range_with_shape` at `crates/ql-exec/src/env.rs:144-189`, which populates `for row { for col { out.push(...) } }` — row-major (left-to-right within a row, then row-by-row). For `A1:B2` the order is `A1, B1, A2, B2`. **This matches Excel's CONCAT canon.** But the doc comment on line 1374 just says "row-major order" without explaining what that means for a 2D range. The test `concat_flattens_range` (line 2644) uses a 1×N range, so it doesn't exercise the 2D semantics. A future contributor refactoring `read_range_with_shape` could silently flip this to column-major and only smoke tests on real sheets would catch it.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:712:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:57:**Severity rationale:** No correctness bug — the behavior is correct under the current code path. NaN-k in particular: a refactor that moves the bound check below the `pos.floor() as usize` cast (which is `0` for NaN, not a panic in safe-cast Rust) would silently return `sorted[0]` instead of `#NUM!` — a real correctness regression that would slip through.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:713:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-11-opus.md:65:**Detail:** Per Codex's documentation review (citing Microsoft TRUNC + QUARTILE.INC docs), Excel truncates a fractional `quart` argument toward zero (TRUNC, not FLOOR). The current implementation uses `n.trunc() as i64` — **correct per Microsoft canon**. But the test suite only pins the positive-fractional case (`quartile_inc_q_truncates_toward_zero`: 2.9 → 2). The negative-fractional case (e.g. `quartile_inc(arr, -0.5)` should return the minimum, NOT `#NUM!`) is NOT pinned. A naive future refactor to `n.floor() as i64` (a plausible misreading of "truncated") would silently change behavior on a sliver of input space without test failure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:718:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:50:Findings: **0 HIGH, 2 MEDIUM, 5 LOW**. Both MEDIUMs are IronCalc-parity divergences that the implementing instance flagged in code but the matrix-doc/test fixtures pin as the v1 behavior. Pattern prediction (1-2H for iterative kernel) does NOT hold — the iterative kernel is well-bounded by both 100-iter and 50-iter caps and a finite-check Err short-circuit. This is a tighter implementation than W5-D-4's BINOM.INV / W5-D-5's GAMMA.INV iterative kernels (which produced Codex HIGHs); the XIRR fallback ladder (Newton-from-guess → bisection → Newton-from-200) is more defensive than either.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:719:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-7-opus.md:178:The iterative kernel is the cleanest of the Wave 3 iterative paths (W5-D-4 BINOM.INV and W5-D-5 GAMMA.INV both produced Codex HIGHs around iteration bounds). XIRR's three-layer fallback ladder (Newton-from-guess → bisection → Newton-from-200) is bounded on every layer, and the `is_finite()` short-circuit makes adversarial paths exit early rather than chase NaN/inf around the function space. The added `f_prime == 0` guard in `xirr_newton` is a strict improvement over IronCalc.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:721:docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.6-design-codex-review.txt:37:The doc also needs explicit rejection behavior for mixed-sheet two-endpoint ranges such as `Sheet1!A1:Sheet2!B2` and future 3D ranges such as `Sheet1:Sheet3!A1`. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:854:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:185:`NamedEntry` at `qbook_format.rs:363–377` does NOT have `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`, while `WorkbookEnvelope` (line 248) and `SheetEnvelope` (line 301) both do. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:856:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:247:This is currently low-impact because `NamedTarget::Formula` entries are not fully surfaced in the formula-evaluation path (deferred to Phase 3+). The comment says "today named formulas are deferred" but does not document this as a known gap or file a follow-up issue. Severity: MEDIUM (latent correctness gap, not a current user-visible crash).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:859:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.6-closing-megaudit-sonnet.md:379:The four MEDIUM findings are all latent (no current crash or data-loss in the happy path) and address areas where the implementation silently diverges from the design doc or creates footguns for future contributors. The overall implementation quality is high: the core parser-workbook decoupling, two-tier name chain, schema v5 save/load, replay reconciliation, and formula-text rewrite on rename are all correctly implemented.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:885:docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-3-opus.md:211:**Severity rationale:** HIGH because (a) the plan checklist explicitly enumerated this coverage class; (b) the no-eval guarantee is the SINGLE most important contract for `ArgContract::LazyShape` (the design's HIGH-B closure); (c) the regression risk is high — a future materializer refactor that "for consistency" applies eager-eval to LazyShape args would silently break the contract; (d) the current `isref_of_divide_by_zero_returns_false_without_eval` test only catches the case where eval would surface an error — it does NOT catch the case where eval succeeds but writes to the cache or fires side effects. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1061:docs/audits/2026-05-14-phase-4.7.H-sonnet-review.md:110:The register loop computes `MAX_ROW + 1` as `u32` — no overflow (MAX_ROW = 1_048_575, u32::MAX = 4_294_967_295) — but it inserts a target entry for a logically out-of-bounds row. The storage layer silently accepts this. This is intentional per design, but a test documenting the behavior (even just asserting the registration succeeds and a target at `MAX_ROW+1` exists in the map) would lock in the "storage is bounds-agnostic" contract so a future reviewer doesn't add accidental defensive clamping.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1064:docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5-d-12-opus.md:104:- **Detail:** Both engine `scalar_fns::counta` and IronCalc `subtotal_counta` count errors (engine: `!matches!(v, Value::Blank).count()` includes Error; IronCalc: `String | Number | Boolean | Error => counta += 1`). Behavior matches. **However**, this is NOT pinned by any SUBTOTAL test — the `subtotal_counta_function_num_3` test only covers `[1, "skip", 2, blank, 3]` (no error). A future refactor of `scalar_fns::counta` to skip errors would silently break compatibility with IronCalc + Excel canon (Excel COUNTA does count errors) and the engine-wide aggregate convention. Probe-verified: `SUBTOTAL(3, [1, #DIV/0!, 3]) = ?`. **Not tested** in the new SUBTOTAL block (probe-confirmed = 3.0 — passes through to counta which counts the error).

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-19-phase-5-6-v1-codex.md:1632:docs/audits/2026-05-13-w5-49-50-51-megaudit-sonnet.md:152:However, as noted in the brief: Phase 3.3 sets `range.sheet = Some(_)` always during binding, so the `unwrap_or(fs)` fallback is currently unreachable. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit.md:64:The module doc claims fingerprints are stable across engine versions. `DefaultHasher`'s contract explicitly says "*The internal algorithm is not specified, and so its instances should not be relied upon over releases.*" Two agents flagged this. Within the pinned `1.95.0` toolchain, fingerprints are deterministic across runs; once the toolchain bumps, every fingerprint value silently shifts. There is also **no golden-fingerprint test** — only relative-equality tests — so a silent shift wouldn't trip CI.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit.md:80:`DivScalar` is lowered to `mul by 1.0/scalar`. So `1/0 → Inf → sanitize_f64(Inf) = #NUM!`. Excel canon: `1/0 = #DIV/0!`. A test at `simd.rs:223-231` pins the wrong-error-class behavior. Per the no-fallbacks rule and Phase 2A.6 audit's emphasis on correct error CLASSES, this is HIGH.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit.md:84:### H6 — Stale sheet id (saved formula refs deleted sheet) silently reads `Value::Blank` instead of `#REF!` ✅ CLOSED 2A.7
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit.md:87:A formula authored against `Sheet3!A1` in a workbook now with 2 sheets binds to `ExprPlan::CellRef { sheet: 2, ... }`, which `WorkbookEnv::read_cell` maps to `Value::Blank`. The env.rs comment admits this is a deferred semantic ("Phase 3+ FormulaRegion binder"). Two agents flagged it. The same agents flagged that `Phase 2A.6` already established the pattern (`NamedTargetIsBlank`, `NamedTargetIsError`) for surfacing previously-silent paths.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit.md:112:### H10 — Bench machine reporter silently falls back on `QBOOK_CHUNK_ROWS` parse failure ✅ CLOSED 2A.7
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit.md:122:The storage-side version (`ql-storage/src/column.rs:35-52`) panics loudly on parse failure, explicitly *because* "prior behavior silently defaulted on any parse failure, which would let a misconfigured A7 chunk-size sweep benchmark the wrong chunk size while pretending to test another." The bench reporter re-introduces the exact bug for its output column. The two env-var paths disagree on policy.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit.md:139:- **M5** ✅ CLOSED 2A.7 — `FunctionRegistry::register` silently overwrites duplicates AND doesn't canonicalize case. Now asserts upper-case names + rejects duplicates with panics. Five new tests pin the contract. (`ql-functions/src/registry.rs:38-40, 104`)
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-12-megaudit.md:165:Long tail: ~30 items including phase-marker rot ("Phase 0 W4-3", "W4-4 will surface"), naming inconsistencies (`set_*` runtime vs `put_*` transaction), 13 stub-crate docstrings claiming "Phase 0 work lands" when Phase 0 closed, loose `is_err()` test assertions, missing test coverage for the `WorkbookTransaction` 10k-op stress case, `0+0`/`-0` fingerprint divergence, parenthesized range pairs `(A:B):(C:D)` silently merging, `LexError::InvalidNumber` misused for "row 0", and various module-doc updates needed.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-session-final-megaudit-sonnet.md:53:This fails silently with `#VALUE!` instead of a clear "CHOOSE does not support range args." The gotchas list in `audit-protocol.md` mentions this briefly under gotcha #6 but doesn't name CHOOSE explicitly. A user writing `=CHOOSE(1, TableA, TableB)` (a common Excel pattern) gets a cryptic `#VALUE!` with no diagnostic.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-session-final-megaudit-sonnet.md:55:**Not a correctness regression** — the current V1 behavior is intentional — but the audit protocol gotchas should explicitly name CHOOSE as a function that's in `is_aggregate_function` for binder-compat reasons yet silently rejects Range args at eval time.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-session-final-megaudit-sonnet.md:104:The MATCH type=1 approximate algorithm uses `break` on the first `Greater` comparison. This is documented as "assumes ascending sort; linear for now." The break is only valid for sorted data — on unsorted data it gives wrong answers silently. The doc comment says "un-sorted input yields undefined results per Excel canon," which is correct. But there's no test asserting that unsorted input gives either `#N/A` or a documented wrong answer. Low risk since Excel itself gives undefined results on unsorted MATCH.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-session-final-megaudit-sonnet.md:206:4. **The CHOOSE footgun pattern** (registered range-aware, silently rejects Range at eval) is not in the gotchas list explicitly. Should add: "CHOOSE is range-aware for binder-compat but returns `#VALUE!` for Range args — common user pattern `=CHOOSE(1, NamedRange1, NamedRange2)` silently fails."
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:26:### HIGH-1 — Range-aware binder admission gap: 31 fns silently unreachable via the named-range path the binder claims to support
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:80:**Severity rationale:** HIGH. The matrix overclaims reach for 28+ user-facing fns. The natural Excel usage path is broken silently with a confusing error message. The fix is mechanical (one name list extension + one invariant strengthening + a handful of e2e tests). The cost of the gap is real product-use failure; the cost of the fix is a single closure commit.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:241:**Severity rationale:** MEDIUM. Excel-compat divergence for a simple use case. Not crashy; not silent. The asymmetry within the same fn family is the load-bearing issue — a maintainer reading `bin2dec` 6 months from now would reasonably expect `collect_base_decode_arg`-style coercion.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:304:The divergence is documented but not pinned by a test. A future refactor that walks `ExprPlan` to detect nested-SUBTOTAL calls (a legitimate path forward toward Excel parity) would silently change behavior. The test would catch the engine→Excel transition.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-phase-4-10-megaudit-opus.md:318:**Detail:** The test iterates over a HARDCODED list of names and asserts each is in the registry. If `is_aggregate_function` adds a new name that ISN'T in the hardcoded list (or vice versa), the test silently passes. There's no introspection on the matcher itself.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-consolidated.md:14:- HIGH-1: Table repair mis-handles auto-disambig'd canonicals → silent formula corruption.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-4-consolidated.md:26:The clean fix would have been to thread the auto-disambig outcome through replay → repair (Opus's suggested option a), but that requires replay API changes. quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-13-phase-4.5-megaudit-codex.txt:5:Phase 4.5 is not clean. The core 1900/1904 conversion module is mostly solid, and the context-aware registry tier is wired correctly, but the date-function layer has two real correctness problems: `ISOWEEKNUM` fails valid lower-bound dates whose ISO-week anchor falls before the workbook epoch, and `YEARFRAC(..., 0)` now contradicts the newly shipped `DAYS360(..., FALSE)` implementation even though both are supposed to represent US/NASD 30/360 semantics. There are also several medium-risk scope and consistency gaps: serial `0` is invalid for `serial_to_ymd(0, Excel1900)` but some higher-level date functions accept it silently; `WorkbookEnv` snapshots `date_system`; `GAP-T-01` is still open despite being targeted at Phase 4.5.A; and the coverage waiver list got worse.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:25:For eager reference-aware functions, the materializer suppresses value reads only for direct reference shapes such as `CellRef`, `RangeRef`, `AggregateNameRef`, and `StructuredRef`. Other shapes still evaluate through `eval_scalar_with_cache` and can depend on nested values or propagate nested errors. For example, `ROW(A1+1)` or `ROWS(IF(A1, B1, C1))` is not a pure coordinate query in the current dispatcher: the fallback path evaluates the binary/function argument before wrapping the result as `Scalar` or `Error`. The calcgraph walker would skip those argument subtrees completely, so edits to `A1`, `B1`, or `C1` can leave the formula stale.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:34:- For scalar fallback shapes such as binary, unary, and nested function plans in eager contracts, recurse normally because the dispatcher evaluates them.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:38:Add calcgraph tests covering direct-cell suppression, scalar fallback dependencies, named-range retargeting, and structured-reference table changes.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:54:The eager materializer later turns a structured reference into `RefArg::Range` through `narrow_structured_ref`. Therefore a top-level formula such as `ROW(Sales[Qty])` or `COLUMN(Sales[Qty])` can bypass the boundary guard and execute with only the materialized range coordinates. If the Step 2 implementation returns the top-left row/column, this recreates the silent truncation behavior the design is trying to prevent.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:111:- Eager materializer output for `CellRef`, `RangeRef`, `AggregateNameRef`, `StructuredRef`, `Array`, `Error`, and scalar fallback.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-rt-step-1-codex.md:113:- Calcgraph walker tests proving direct reference values are suppressed but scalar fallback and structural name/table dependencies are retained.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:14:The V2 V3 step 1-4 arc is correct on the happy paths exercised by the 4433-test gate, but its **silent-loss surface** is wider than the docs admit. The single most likely production-visible failure is `WebSocketTransport::Drop` discarding queued outbound bytes the caller has already been told are "queued for send" (trait contract: `send` returns when bytes are queued, not delivered). For an IDE consumer that auto-flushes the last op and then closes the workbook tab, that last delta vanishes on the wire — peer never sees it — and `has_pending_flush()` already reports false because the local VV was advanced. The offline-write story does NOT recover this case (it depends on `last_flushed_vv` rollback, which never happened).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:16:Secondary defensive concerns cluster around (a) two silent-error swallows that violate CLAUDE.md no-fallback (poisoned `last_error` mutex, dropped reader-task `inbound_tx.send` `is_err()`), (b) one race in the test fixture (EchoServer accept→push under separate locks) that could leak per-conn tasks past test end on adverse interleaving, and (c) a panic-in-task gap: tokio runtime swallows panics in spawned tasks, the `closed` flag is set only on `Err` arms, so a panicked reader/writer leaves the transport in `closed = false` state with no tasks running — caller polls `try_recv` forever returning `Ok(None)`.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:18:None of these are HIGH because each requires a corner-case interleaving or a panic that the current code doesn't appear to produce. But the audit prompt asks "where will future changes silently break invariants?" — and the answers here are concentrated, not diffuse. Codex's protocol lane and Opus-A's IDE round-trip lane should cross-validate the M1 finding in particular (drop-loss).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:24:### M1 — `WebSocketTransport::Drop` silently discards queued-but-unsent bytes; offline-write story does not recover them
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:48:V2 V4 reconnect work already accepts this gap implicitly (full delta-from-empty-VV resend recovers everything Loro knows about). But the no-reconnect case (tab close mid-flush) is silently lossy and should be either pinned in a test as ACCEPTED behavior or addressed.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:76:### M3 — Poisoned `last_error` mutex silently returns `None` — violates CLAUDE.md no-fallback rule
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:88:Per CLAUDE.md no-fallback: "No try/catch that swallows errors or returns a default value. No `value || default` patterns." `.lock().ok().and_then(...)` is exactly that pattern.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:90:The same shape exists in both writer and reader tasks at lines 266 and 310: `if let Ok(mut slot) = last_error_writer.lock() { ... }`. A poisoned mutex on the producer side means the error is silently dropped. Likelier than the reader side because the writer task is the one that's more likely to panic (allocator for `bytes.into()`).
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:157:The defensive concern is documentation: a future maintainer migrating to async Mutex would silently introduce a leak.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:186:### L1 — Reader task's `inbound_tx.send(bytes.to_vec()).is_err()` returns silently without setting `closed`
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-21-phase-5-5-v2-v3-step-5-opus-b.md:220:The Send assert covers `WebSocketTransport`. The `WebSocketError` type derives `Clone, Error`. It's `Send + Sync` only because all its fields are `String` — not pinned. If a future refactor adds an `Arc<dyn FnOnce>` or similar to `RuntimeError`, the type silently becomes `!Send` and `last_error()` (which returns `Option<WebSocketError>`) still compiles. Future cross-thread `last_error()` consumers would discover the regression downstream.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-self.md:114:**Subject:** OOXML parsers use `attr.unescape_value().unwrap_or_default()` for required attributes, silently converting parse failures to empty strings.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-self.md:118:**Detail:** Per CLAUDE.md no-fallbacks rule, malformed OOXML should surface errors loudly. Example: `attr.unescape_value().unwrap_or_default().to_string()` for the `name` attribute of `<sheet>` returns `""` on UTF-8 decode failure, which then passes the `if name.is_empty()` malformed-check — but only because we happen to check `is_empty()`. Sites without such follow-up checks silently corrupt.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-17-w5183-vdb-codex.md:43:OpenFormula's VDB constraints require `Salvage < Cost`, and LibreOffice's VDB wrapper rejects `fSalvage > fCost` before calculation. This should be `#NUM!`, not silent zero depreciation.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-3-step-2-opus.md:34:**What**: Step 2 silently delegates ALL non-case-1 paths to `Workbook::rename_sheet(id, new_name.clone())`. `Workbook::rename_sheet` at `workbook.rs:497-499` returns `SheetNameError::Empty` when `new_name.is_empty()`. Pre-step-2 producer-side validation in `WorkbookRuntime::rename_sheet` rejects empty names — but the wire op format does not enforce this.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-megaudit-opus-c.md:11:**Phase 4.11 should ship.** v1 is structurally honest: features it can't preserve are surfaced via `dropped_features` rather than silently lost, and the v2 deferral set (rels-graph merge for sheet-anchored parts, sheet-inline-anchor merge, `xfId/cellStyleXfs` preservation) is well-defined and tracked. The current `PartAction` enum and the post-process zip walk in `umya_export::post_process_zip` are the right shape to extend.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-11-megaudit-opus-c.md:31:There are 18 separate `text.find` / `text.replace` / `text.rfind` calls. Each mutation pattern has its own custom edge-case handling (self-closing vs long-form tag, ordering of `</tag>`-first-then-`/>`-fallback, etc.). Several have already shipped real bugs caught in audits:
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:49:### H-2. `WorkbookRuntime::recompute_all` silently produces wrong values for cyclic formulas (no #CIRC! emission)
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:68:- A `=A1+1` formula in cell A1 evaluates to `1.0` on `set_formula`, then `2.0` on first `recompute_all`, then `3.0` on the next, etc. Every recompute mutates the value. This is silent corruption — there is no #CIRC! error to alert the user.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:70:- The module docstring (`crates/ql-exec/src/workbook_runtime.rs:16`) describes `recompute_all` as "legacy HashMap-order full pass; no graph awareness" but does not mention the silent-cycle consequence. Callers reading the doc cannot infer "if your workbook has a cycle you will get garbage numbers instead of #CIRC!".
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:72:**Fix sketch (no-fallback compliant):** Either (a) make `recompute_all` panic-loud-fail when a self-reference / cycle is detectable cheaply (e.g., a single-formula-references-its-own-cell guard), or (b) deprecate `recompute_all` and force replay callers through `recompute_dirty`, OR (c) keep behavior but document it explicitly with the silent-corruption consequence called out. Option (c) alone is the bare minimum — current docs hide the failure mode.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:98:### H-4. Lexer accepts NUL (`\u{00}`) inside string literals — silent data smuggling into round-trip output
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:110:  - Truncate strings when passed to C bindings (`ql-bindings-c/`) — silent data loss on the boundary.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:135:**Symptom:** `recompute_all` has special-cased `UnknownTable` / `UnknownTableColumn` to emit `#NAME?` (a previously-closed HIGH from W5-156), proving that the legacy path can map a bind-time error to a typed sigil. The same special-case is **not** present for self-references / cycles, so cycles silently produce numerics (see H-2). The fix shape exists in the codebase already; cycles just weren't included.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:160:**Why M:** The envelope is TOML which is largely whitespace-tolerant, so dropping a trailing newline (typical "last byte") still parses. The bigger picture: there's no envelope-level checksum, so a flipped byte in the *middle* of `workbook.toml` that happens to keep TOML syntactically valid would load to a silently-wrong workbook. The existing two-phase load (`SchemaVersionProbe` first, then `WorkbookEnvelope` with `deny_unknown_fields`) is good defense against schema drift but not against value corruption.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-phase-4-12-megaudit-opus-b.md:169:**Files:** `crates/ql-formula-syntax/tests/p412_defensive_fuzz_probes.rs` — the `try_parse` wrapper uses `panic::catch_unwind` but doesn't isolate to a separate thread. When `deep_function_call_1000` overflows the test-binary main-thread stack, the whole binary aborts — no assertion ever runs, and all subsequent tests in the file silently skip. Engineering note for future fuzz work: every recursion probe must run inside a `thread::Builder::default().spawn(...)` so the overflow is contained.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-7-codex.md:47:1. **MAGIC collision risk with Loro snapshot prefix.** Loro snapshots have their own internal format header — what's its first 4 bytes? If Loro snapshots can start with `b"QLOL"` (extremely unlikely but worth verifying), the legacy detection path silently mis-routes. Verify by inspecting `loro` crate's snapshot magic OR by exporting a sample snapshot and inspecting bytes 0..4.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-7-codex.md:49:2. **Empty-file boundary.** New test `tier_d3_empty_oplog_bin_routes_to_legacy_path_and_loro_errors` asserts empty file → legacy path → OpLog error. Verify the assertion is correct: `OpLog::import_bytes(b"")` indeed errors (not succeeds with an empty log). If empty bytes succeed, a corrupted-to-empty file would silently load as an empty op log — silent loss.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-7-codex.md:431:quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-20-phase-5-2-d-1-step-4-opus.md:13:**M1 — Commit message and d-1 checklist do not call out the oplog.bin wire-format break.** The commit message lists deliverables but never says "any pre-step-4 `oplog.bin` saved by an earlier build will fail to deserialize post-step-4 until step 7 ships the magic-byte / schema-version envelope." Mitigation: (a) confirmed no `.bin` fixture files exist anywhere outside `target/` and `.references/`; (b) Loro snapshot reload of a pre-step-4 export would fail at the `serde_json::from_str::<Op>` boundary with a useful `OpLogError::Deserialize` (visible error, no silent corruption). So no production data is at risk yet; this is a documentation/scoping nit, but worth one line in step 7's commit message.

quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-codex.md:99:**Subject:** Table XML parser silently accepts malformed required numeric attributes and invalid table metadata
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-codex.md:103:**Detail:** `id`, `headerRowCount`, `totalsRowCount`, and `tableColumn/@id` parse failures fall back to `0`/defaults. The parser does not validate `tableColumns/@count`, column count vs `ref` width, duplicate/zero column ids, duplicate table names, or table footprint bounds. `TableTable::insert` overwrites on canonical-name collision, so malformed duplicate tables silently lose one table.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-codex.md:107:**Severity rationale:** Corrupt OOXML should surface visible errors at the XLSX trust boundary; current behavior silently mutates table structure.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-codex.md:159:**Subject:** OOXML parsers silently swallow malformed attributes
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-codex.md:163:**Detail:** Multiple parsers use `attributes().with_checks(false).flatten()` plus `unescape_value().unwrap_or_default()`. This drops malformed attributes instead of surfacing XML/OOXML errors. In workbook defined names, a malformed `localSheetId` is silently treated as workbook-scoped. In rels parsing, a relationship with missing `Type`/`Target` but nonempty `Id` is accepted.
quantbook-engine/docs/audits/2026-05-18-w5-d-14-codex.md:179:**Severity rationale:** Sheet identity and visibility are workbook structure, not cosmetic metadata, and currently they can silently diverge.
